title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Fractal Geometry
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization is a burgeoning field aiming to emulate the behavior of quantum algorithms to accelerate computationally intensive optimization problems. This paper explores the application of fractal geometry to enhance the efficiency of optimization techniques, proposing a novel approach that leverages fractal representations to create a more complex search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through the analysis of a challenging, non-convex optimization problem, showcasing significant improvements in convergence and solution quality compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around the construction of a fractal search space, which, through the application of specific fractal operations, facilitates a more efficient exploration of the solution space. This investigation provides a foundational understanding of how fractal geometry can be effectively integrated into optimization to overcome limitations inherent in conventional approaches.

title: Carolina Flying Squirrel Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Locomotion of the Carolina Flying Squirrel
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Carolina Flying Squirrel Algorithm (CFSA), inspired by the unique locomotion strategies of the Carolina flying squirrel ( *Glaucomys sabrinus*). The algorithm leverages the squirrel's ability to dynamically adjust its trajectory, utilizing a combination of gliding, leaping, and controlled descent to navigate complex environments. CFSA employs a population-based search strategy where individuals represent potential solutions. Movement within the population is governed by a dynamic velocity update mechanism, mirroring the squirrel's adjustment of its flight path based on environmental factors and momentum. A novel 'risk assessment' component, mimicking the squirrel's cautious approach to landing, is introduced to guide the search towards promising regions of the solution space. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative application of biological inspiration to create a robust and adaptable metaheuristic algorithm. The mathematical formulation of the core components of CFSA is presented, including the velocity update equation and the risk assessment function. The algorithm demonstrates competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) in several test cases.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks: Adaptive Mapping Mechanisms
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-organizing neural networks (SONNs) incorporating adaptive mapping mechanisms to enhance performance. Traditional neural network architectures often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the model's capacity and potential for optimization. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing adaptive mapping to dynamically adjust network parameters, thereby improving model efficacy. We explore a framework where the network's parameters are adjusted based on a learned mapping function, allowing for a more nuanced and responsive optimization process. The core claim centers on the efficacy of this adaptive mapping mechanism in boosting performance across a range of tasks. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the proposed framework, including mathematical formulations and illustrative examples, demonstrating the potential of this approach to advance the capabilities of SONNs.

title: Adaptive Probabilistic Programming for Scientific Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic programming, termed Adaptive Probabilistic Programming (APP), designed to address the limitations of traditional, static systems in scientific discovery. The core idea is to dynamically adapt the probabilistic programming language itself based on the evolving nature of the data and the model's performance. This adaptation is achieved through a compiler that continuously monitors model evidence, parameter uncertainty, and other statistical metrics. Based on this monitoring, the compiler automatically modifies the model by adding or removing variables, constraints, or even switching inference algorithms. This dynamic refinement process enables real-time model exploration and discovery, particularly valuable in complex scientific domains where models are often iteratively refined as new data emerges. The system's ability to adapt in real-time represents a significant shift from static probabilistic programming, promising to accelerate the process of model building and scientific insight.

title: Brown Titi Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Brown Titi Algorithm (BTA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brown Titi monkey ( *Maconochita tonduisi* ). BTA leverages the monkey's dynamic exploration and exploitation strategies for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates a unique combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel population maintenance mechanism, and a modified Lévy flight navigation strategy. We present the algorithm's theoretical foundations, detailing its core components and operational rules. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and computational efficiency. The results indicate that BTA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios demanding adaptive exploration and exploitation. Further research will focus on extending BTA to handle multi-objective optimization and real-world engineering applications.

title: 拓扑量子纠缠的理论化建模
abstract: The study of quantum entanglement, traditionally focused on the superposition of quantum states, holds the potential to extend beyond simple quantum states to encompass complex topological structures. This paper explores the theoretical modeling of quantum entanglement through the lens of topology, proposing a novel framework for quantum information processing. We argue that the inherent properties of topological spaces offer a unique computational landscape, allowing for the encoding, manipulation, and optimization of quantum information at a fundamental level. The core claim centers on the development of a computational framework that leverages topological structures to achieve global quantum information optimization. This work represents a significant departure from traditional approaches, offering a potentially transformative pathway for quantum computation.

title: Bornean Slow Loris-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Loris Optimization Algorithm" (LOA), inspired by the foraging behavior and strategic decision-making processes observed in Bornean slow lorises. These animals are known for their deliberate and adaptive approach to food acquisition, often employing a "look-then-leap" strategy combined with cautious exploration. The LOA leverages these principles to effectively navigate complex optimization landscapes. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search, similar to particle swarm optimization, but incorporates a 'risk assessment' mechanism mimicking the lorises' cautious approach. This mechanism dynamically adjusts the exploration and exploitation balance, preventing premature convergence and promoting robustness. The core innovation lies in the introduction of a 'momentum' term influenced by the lorises' tendency to maintain a certain direction while adapting to new information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the LOA through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, showcasing its potential application across a range of optimization problems, including continuous optimization, combinatorial optimization, and function optimization. The LOA's performance is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) to highlight its advantages in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and robustness. Finally, we discuss potential future research directions and extensions of the LOA.

title: Temporal Logic for Quantum State Evolution
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state evolution by leveraging temporal logic formalisms. The core idea is to directly represent and reason about quantum state transitions, incorporating the inherent uncertainties of non-deterministic branching and measurement outcomes. We propose a new temporal logic variant, Temporal Probabilistic Logic (TPL), where quantum state transitions are defined as logical rules and measurement collapses are modeled as probabilistic branches within the temporal reasoning process. This purely logical framework contrasts with traditional numerical simulation methods used in quantum control theory, offering potential advantages in automated proof of correctness, algorithm design, and optimization. TPL allows for the formal specification of quantum protocols and the verification of their behavior without relying on computationally intensive simulations. The paper outlines the key components of TPL, including its syntax, semantics, and operational rules, and explores its application to a simplified quantum algorithm. The presented framework provides a foundation for developing a more robust and verifiable approach to quantum computation.

abstract: A user-friendly interactive Shiny interface for the 'BsplineQuantReg' package, enabling quantile regression using B-splines with shape constraints, based on the method described in Abbes (2025).Almost all parameters of the main function 'quantile_spline()' can be tuned.Features include interactive knot placement, per-region constraint specification, 'CSV' data import, direct demo access, reproducible R code generation, and solver selection.The version 0.2.2 handles knots multiplicity, Bspline basis visualisation, meansquare regression, pp form visualisation under human readable form, in local or canonical bases, The GUI provides two modes, basic (compatible with 'BsplineQuantReg' >= 0.2.2) and advanced (requires 'BsplineQuantReg' >= 0.2.5 for stable multiplicity features).This GUI an improved version of the 'Python Tk' version of 'BsplineQuantRegPy'.

title: Cognitive Model for Control of a Peltier Element
abstract: Abstract— The article presents an ontological model of a control system for a Peltier element. The ontology describes the structure of the system by identifying objects, transformation processes within these objects, and the attributes of the relationships between them. Based on the developed ontological model, a cascade control system has been designed, integrating a PID controller, a fuzzy-digital filter, and an exponentially weighted moving average filter (EWMAF), with its cognitive behavior based on fuzzy logic rules. Improvement of the dynamic characteristics of transient processes in the Peltier element control system is achieved through the use of the model of mathematical and ontological solutions. The cascade control system reduces the amplitude of the first harmonic of the control signal by 12% and reduces the settling time by 31.9%.

title: Adaptive-batch stochastic gradient descent for constrained optimization based on relaxed barrier functions
abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is the cornerstone of large-scale optimization; however, its application to problems with a vast number of constraints remains a significant challenge. Methods based on relaxed logarithmic barrier functions have enabled the use of SGD by sampling constraints, yet the reliance on single samples in these methods often leads to high variance and oscillations that hinder progress near the optimal solution.In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid algorithm, AdaBS-RBSGD, which integrates the relaxed barrier framework with an adaptive batch size strategy. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the batch size Bk to be inversely proportional to the estimated optimization loss, systematically reducing gradient variance as the iterations approach the solution.We provide a rigorous mathematical proof establishing the almost-sure convergence of this hybrid algorithm. Furthermore, our theoretical analysis of error bounds demonstrates that active variance management allows the error term associated with stochastic noise to vanish more rapidly compared to the baseline method. Empirically, results on a benchmark problem show that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms its single-sample counterpart, successfully breaking the “noise floor,” achieving higher stability, and reaching a more accurate final solution. This work presents a practical and theoretically sound methodology for accelerating and improving the precision of stochastic constrained optimization.

title: Comparative Analysis of CBOW and Skip-Gram Models for Uzbek Literary Corpus Embeddings
abstract: Word embeddings remain computationally accessible tools for representing lexical relations in low-resource and morphologically rich languages. However, the agglutinative structure of Uzbek distributes lexical information across numerous suffixed surface forms, which may affect vocabulary coverage and embedding quality. This study presents a controlled comparison of the Continuous Bag-of-Words (CBOW) and Skip-gram Word2Vec architectures using a literary corpus derived from Abdulla Qodiriy's Uzbek novel O'tkan kunlar. The corpus was processed through case normalization, apostrophe standardization, character filtering, sentence segmentation, whitespace tokenization, and length-based filtering. Stemming, lemmatization, and stop-word removal were not applied; consequently, the models were trained on normalized surface forms. The processed corpus contained 7,607 sentences, 95,448 tokens, and 23,121 unique tokens. Both architectures were trained under identical explicitly defined settings, including 200-dimensional vectors, a maximum context window of seven tokens, a minimum frequency threshold of one, 50 epochs, and ten negative samples. The embedding spaces were evaluated using nearest-neighbor retrieval, pairwise cosine similarity, K-means-based internal clustering metrics, and PCA and t-SNE visualizations. Under the same local computational environment, CBOW completed training in 1.49 seconds, compared with 2.97 seconds for Skip-gram. For the lexical pairs inson–odam and dard–g'am, CBOW produced cosine similarity scores of 0.916 and 0.841, whereas Skip-gram produced 0.563 and 0.603. CBOW also obtained comparatively more favorable clustering results: a Silhouette Score of 0.0521, a Davies–Bouldin Index of 2.4598, and a Calinski–Harabasz Score of 766.16. The corresponding Skip-gram values were −0.0410, 4.3396, and 301.31. The nearest-neighbor results showed that both models captured corpus-specific relations involving literary characters, thematic vocabulary, and recurrent narrative contexts. However, the low absolute Silhouette values indicate substantial overlap between the generated clusters. The findings therefore demonstrate a relative advantage for CBOW under the investigated configuration rather than its universal superiority for Uzbek. The study establishes a surface-form Word2Vec baseline for future comparison with morphologically informed, subword-based, and contextual embedding approaches for Uzbek NLP.

Both architectures were trained under identical explicitly defined settings, including 200-dimensional vectors, a maximum context window of seven tokens, a minimum frequency threshold of one, 50 epochs, and ten negative samples. The embedding spaces were evaluated using nearest-neighbor retrieval, pairwise cosine similarity, K-means-based internal clustering metrics, and PCA and t-SNE visualizations. Under the same local computational environment, CBOW completed training in 1.49 seconds, compared with 2.97 seconds for Skip-gram. For the lexical pairs inson–odam and dard–g'am, CBOW produced cosine similarity scores of 0.916 and 0.841, whereas Skip-gram produced 0.563 and 0.603. CBOW also obtained comparatively more favorable clustering results: a Silhouette Score of 0.0521, a Davies–Bouldin Index of 2.4598, and a Calinski–Harabasz Score of 766.16. The corresponding Skip-gram values were −0.0410, 4.3396, and 301.31. The nearest-neighbor results showed that both models captured corpus-specific relations involving literary characters, thematic vocabulary, and recurrent narrative contexts. However, the low absolute Silhouette values indicate substantial overlap between the generated clusters. The findings therefore demonstrate a relative advantage for CBOW under the investigated configuration rather than its universal superiority for Uzbek. The study establishes a surface-form Word2Vec baseline for future comparison with morphologically informed, subword-based, and contextual embedding approaches for Uzbek NLP.

title: Restricted Boltzmann machines in physics: concepts, theories and applications
abstract: Abstract A restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) is a two-layer neural-network machine-learning model comprising a visible layer that represents observed data and a hidden layer that captures correlations among the visible units. Rooted in ideas from statistical mechanics, RBMs provide a probabilistic framework for modeling complex, high-dimensional distributions through an energy function and a corresponding Boltzmann distribution. This review offers an accessible introduction to RBMs from a physics-oriented perspective, focusing on their core concepts and training principles. We survey key theoretical developments that interpret RBMs as many-body systems, highlighting their equilibrium/non-equilibrium thermodynamics, learning dynamics, mean-field properties, phase diagrams, and free energy calculation. We further discuss recent applications of RBMs to a range of physics problems, including quantum-mechanical wavefunction representation, statistical-mechanical Boltzmann distribution modeling, and biological protein sequence analysis.

title: Explainable Tri-Stream CNN-Transformer-Geometric Fusion for High-Precision Gynecological Malignancies Classification
abstract: Automated classification of gynecological malignancies from cytological and histopathological images remains a critical yet challenging clinical problem. This task is complicated by inter-class morphological similarity, intra-class heterogeneity, and class imbalance. Furthermore, single-stream architectures may have limited capacity to simultaneously capture fine-grained local morphology, long-range tissue context, and rotation-invariant structural geometry. This paper proposes a tri-stream deep learning framework that integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN), a DeiT-III encoder, and an Angular-Radial Partitioning (ARP) descriptor within a unified multi-stream fusion architecture for gynecological malignancy recognition. The CNN pathway extracts hierarchically structured local morphological features including nuclei boundaries, stromal textures, and micro-architectural patterns. The DeiT-III transformer captures global contextual dependencies between spatially distant tissue regions through multi-head self-attention operating on CNN-derived semantic tokens. The ARP module generates rotation-invariant geometric descriptors by decomposing the image into polar sectors and aggregating edge energy distributions across radial rings and angular wedges. The three streams are fused via concatenation followed by a dense projection layer regularized with L2 weight decay, and a composite loss function combining categorical cross-entropy with focal loss addresses class imbalance during training. Hyperparameter configuration is automated through Status-Based Optimization (SBO), a population-based metaheuristic that systematically optimizes over a joint search space of learning rate, focal loss weight, regularization coefficients, optimizer selection, and scheduling policy by simulating hierarchical social learning. Moreover, Gray-World Standard Deviation (GWSD) normalization and augmentation-based class balancing are applied as preprocessing and data preparation strategies. Experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets named SIPaKMeD, CIVa, and Mendeley LBC, yielding overall classification accuracies of 97.91%, 99.74%, and 99.48% respectively, with macro-averaged F1-scores of 97.89%, 99.28%, and 99.07%. Ablation, robustness, statistical significance, and cross-validation analyses collectively demonstrate the empirical contribution and complementarity of the architectural components, while GradCAM and LIME analyses indicate that the model emphasizes image regions associated with clinically relevant morphological and tissue-structural patterns.

title: Large language models as digital libraries: a multi-benchmark and multi-model study
abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as flexible access layers for information-rich collections, raising the question of whether they can also support structured access to cultural heritage data as if they were digital libraries. This work investigates that question through Galois, a database-inspired system that treats the LLM as a noisy storage layer. We evaluate six querying modes: direct natural language prompting, direct SQL prompting, and four Galois strategies that combine LLM-facing tuple retrieval with deterministic relational processing. The evaluation uses two cultural heritage benchmarks: Paintings Extended, based on paintings data, and a new benchmark based on Europeana metadata. For both benchmarks, we define fourteen query templates with ten variants each. The main experiments use GPT-4o-mini, Granite 3.3 8B, and Llama 3 70B, with an additional diagnostic analysis of two GPT-5 deployments. We complement the benchmark metrics with a stratified manual audit of 60 unique disagreements. Performance is strongly shaped by model capability, deployment behavior, dataset structure, and execution strategy. Direct natural language prompting is the strongest and most robust baseline, while direct SQL prompting becomes nearly equivalent on the strongest open models. Among the structured strategies, only GaloisA and GaloisF become meaningfully competitive, especially on the flatter Europeana benchmark. In the audited sample, 35 disagreements were model-originated failures, 21 reflected reference-coverage or metadata-normalization effects, and four remained indeterminate. The additional GPT-5 deployment analysis reveals frequent empty outputs and provider-level constraints. These diagnostic results characterize the specific tested deployments and must not be interpreted as a general ranking of GPT-5 model capability. Querying LLMs as digital libraries is feasible, but its effectiveness depends on model strength, deployment conditions, dataset structure, and execution strategy. Direct prompting is already strong for exploratory cultural heritage access, while Galois remains valuable when relational discipline and controlled query execution are required.

title: Training-Free Inpainting Across Domains with a Frozen Text-to-Image Diffusion Model
abstract: We show that a frozen generic text-to-image diffusion model can perform conditional inpainting across three evaluated natural-image domains with one fixed controller configuration, without inpainting-specific weight training, dataset-specific weight adaptation, or learned inpainting-specific conditioning channels. Step-PI augments known-region projection with boundary-interior latent feedback, persistent PI state, and a predefined four-field release schedule that modulates controller signals along the reverse trajectory. Developed only on Main35-disjoint CelebA-HQ pilots, the controller transfers unchanged to AFHQ and Places2. Across two field-identical comparisons on the same 3,500 cases, adding persistent state and replacing uniform release with the predefined schedule each improve all 15 dataset-metric cells; 95% bootstrap intervals exclude zero for all five metrics in both comparisons. In descriptive native-route comparisons, Step-PI leads LanPaint and PILOT (the closest evaluated training-free baselines using vanilla SD1.5) on all five equal-dataset macro metrics. Inpainting-trained systems retain the absolute metric leads but rely on substantial inpainting-specific offline optimization. Our method provides a complementary approach for repurposing a frozen generic text-to-image model for cross-domain inpainting through test-time latent control.

title: PersuaRL: Reinforcement Learning-Driven Multi-Expert Selection for Persuasive Dialogue Generation in Insurance
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are revolutionizing digital communication by powering conversational agents deployed across domains such as customer service, digital sales, and insurance. These agents, built on LLMs, can understand user input, retrieve relevant information, and generate coherent responses. However, while they excel at factual communication, they often lack the ability to engage in truly persuasive, context-sensitive dialogue, especially in domains like insurance, where trust and clarity are critical. Building on this need within the insurance domain, our work focuses on improving the persuasiveness of digital agents, aka LLMs. To support this, we introduce InsureDial, a Persuasive Insurance Dialogue dataset, designed to capture the nuances of persuasive communication specific to motor insurance interactions. We introduce PersuaRL, a reinforcement learning-based framework that equips LLM-driven dialogue agents with the ability to adaptively explore, select, and coordinate strategies across multiple expert modules, guided by the evolving dialogue context, to achieve more effective persuasion. We conduct extensive automatic human and qualitative evaluations on two benchmark persuasion dialogue datasets, including our InsureDial. Our evaluations consistently demonstrate that PersuaRL outperforms baseline, generating contextually appropriate and highly persuasive responses.

title: Measuring Optimal Transport in Transformer Depth
abstract: A transformer carries each token's state from layer to layer, and the whole vocabulary carried together forms a cloud that moves with depth. We ask whether a trained network moves this cloud the way optimal transport would: at the cheapest cost, and along the map that pairs each token with its optimal destination. We measure both on Pythia-160m and Pythia-410m, with an exact assignment between consecutive layer clouds, a measured sampling floor, calibration on couplings known to be optimal, and a split of the cost into the common shift of the cloud and the token-specific moves. At the last layer, both models move their tokens where the optimal-transport map sends them, at the optimal cost for Pythia-410m and slightly above it for Pythia-160m. At the first layer they do not. In between, single layers can be judged on cost at only two of ten transitions, and blocks of several layers move the cloud at close to the optimal cost. The agreement at the last layer is much weaker at initialisation (0.64 against 0.86) and grows with training.

title: Vision-Language-Guided Pseudo-Labels for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Semantic Segmentation for Waste Sorting
abstract: Obtaining labeled data for semantic segmentation in applied settings (e.g., autonomous driving, industrial waste sorting) is expensive and often infeasible at scale. We present a cross-modal pseudo-labeling pipeline that enables unsupervised domain adaptation without any target-domain annotations. The pipeline is built on two core foundation models: SAM generates class-agnostic region proposals, and EVA-CLIP assigns semantic labels based on region-text similarity, with confidence filtering ensuring that only reliable pseudo-labels are used for self-training a segmentation model. As an optional extension, BLIP provides language-grounded verification for ambiguous regions, thereby improving pseudo-label quality without altering the overall pipeline. Evaluated on two domain shifts, synthetic-to-real autonomous driving and, with a primary focus, lab-to-factory industrial waste sorting, the pipeline consistently improves over source-only baselines. Our results demonstrate that pseudo-label quality, not quantity, is a decisive factor in self-training under domain shift, and that cross-modal language grounding offers a practical path to reliable automatic annotation in deployment-critical applications.

title: QINA: Quantum-Inspired Nonlinear Adapters for Pretrained Vision Models
abstract: Adapting large pretrained vision models under limited data and frozen-backbone constraints remains a central challenge in transfer learning. While lightweight adapters and parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods are widely adopted, most rely on generic multilayer perceptrons or low-rank linear updates, offering limited control over the spectral and geometric structure of feature transformations. We investigate whether structured nonlinear feature lifting can improve representational alignment in frozen regimes. We introduce Quantum-Inspired Nonlinear Adapters (QINA), compact modules that perform learnable trigonometric feature lifting followed by bounded nonlinear aggregation. The design induces structured oscillatory basis functions with an explicit norm-dependent Lipschitz bound, enabling spectral reshaping of pretrained representations without increasing the receptive field or significantly expanding parameter count. Importantly, the method operates entirely within standard deep learning frameworks and does not require quantum hardware. Through systematic experiments across natural and medical imaging datasets, classification and segmentation tasks, multiple adapters and placements, and varying training budgets, we show that performance in frozen regimes is primarily representation-limited. Nonlinear lifting improves adaptation, and the proposed structured trigonometric formulation consistently outperforms identity baselines, fixed Fourier feature mappings, and parameter-matched baseline adapters. Within the evaluated frozen-backbone settings, structured spectral parameterization provides a more effective inductive bias than generic nonlinear adapters. This work highlights the importance of geometry- and spectrum-aware adaptation mechanisms for large pretrained vision models.

title: A Federated Learning-Driven Method for Privacy-Preserving Vocational Learner Profiling and Practical Training Path Recommendation
abstract: In vocational education cloud platforms, online training systems, and school-enterprise collaborative training scenarios, vocational learner behavior data are typically distributed across schools, platforms, and training bases, and centralized profiling and pathrecommendation methods that rely on aggregating raw data risk privacy leakage, data silos, and limited scalability. This study proposes FL-PTR, a federated learning-driven method for privacy-preserving vocational learner profiling and practical training path recommendation, enabling cross-client collaborative profile modeling and personalized path recommendation without uploading raw behavior data. FL-PTR comprises a data acquisition layer, local profiling layer, privacy protection layer, federated collaboration layer, path recommendation layer, and feedback update layer; each client locally encodes behavior sequences and uploads protected updates via gradient pruning, differential privacy noise, and secure aggregation, while the server computes trust-aware aggregation weights from client contribution, stability, anomaly risk, and reputation. In a heavily non-IID scenario, FL-PTR achieves an NDCG@10 of 0.628 , a Recall@10 of 0.416 , and a Path Completion Rate of 0.743 , outperforming FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, and DP-FedAvg. With privacy budget ε = 4, membership and attribute inference attack success rates fall to 39.6% and 36.7% while recommendation performance is largely preserved, and performance stays stable as clients scale to 200 and under 30% anomalous clients.

title: Analisis Sentimen Presepsi Masyarakat terhadap Perkembangan dan Kontribusi UMKM di Kabupaten Bulukumba
abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a strategic role in supporting regional economic growth and improving community welfare. However, public perceptions regarding the development and contribution of MSMEs need to be identified to evaluate their role in society. This study aims to analyze the sentiment of MSME actors' perceptions regarding the development and contribution of MSMEs in Bulukumba Regency using the Naïve Bayes algorithm. The research employed a descriptive qualitative approach with sentiment analysis. Primary data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation involving eight culinary MSME owners operating in the Pantai Merpati area, Bulukumba Regency. The interview results were transcribed into textual data and processed through preprocessing stages, including cleaning, tokenizing, filtering, and stemming, before being classified into positive, negative, and neutral sentiment categories using the Naïve Bayes algorithm. title: Quality control methods for global tilted irradiance measurements
abstract: Most solar energy applications that collect solar radiation on flat collectors, such as PV modules or solar thermal panels, use a tilted surface rather than a horizontal one. The tilted surface can be either fixed or tracking (moving to follow the sun's position), with tracking systems offering further energy collection improvements at the cost of increased complexity and maintenance requirements. In all these applications, performance calculations require global tilted irradiance (GTI) measurements. In this work we present two novel methods to perform quality control (QC) on tilted irradiance measurements for meteorological stations that are equipped with separate beam / direct normal (DNI) and diffuse (DHI) or global horizontal (GHI) irradiance measurements. Both QC methods are based on the comparison of measured GTI values with calculated values using a transposition model. The first method serves to calculate dynamic thresholds for anomaly detection by propagating plausible intervals of various inputs through the transposition calculation to obtain an interval of plausible GTI values. The second method serves to detect and check tilt and azimuth angles of the GTI sensor from the measurements. Unlike previous approaches, the orientation check includes an estimation of the check’s uncertainty and acceptance interval. The methods have been used on several high-quality but imperfect data sets and found to provide valuable insights into those imperfections. Although the outlier detection method generates dynamic thresholds for GTI, a number of static thresholds need to be set for the inputs to the transposition model. This gives some flexibility to tune the sensitivity to site-specific conditions. Finally, the method can be adapted to situations where DNI and DHI measurements are not available by using a separation model to estimate them from GHI.

title: Attention Is All You Needed, Eventually: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of transformers and attention as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Caracol Climbing Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Climbing Behavior of Caracolets
abstract: This paper presents Caracol Climbing Rat (CCR), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the unique climbing behavior of Caracolets ( *Oligoryx luculentus*), a species of rodent found in the Caribbean. Caracolets are renowned for their ability to scale steep, muddy cliffs with remarkable speed and efficiency. CCR leverages this behavior through a dynamic exploration-exploitation strategy, employing a 'caracol' movement pattern and a novel 'mud' adaptation mechanism to navigate solution spaces. The algorithm incorporates a population-based approach, utilizing a swarm of 'rats' to iteratively refine solutions. The core innovation lies in the adaptation of a 'mud' parameter that modulates the movement strategy based on the solution's fitness and the local landscape. The effectiveness of CCR is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's performance is quantified using metrics like convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. This research contributes a new approach to metaheuristic design, drawing inspiration from a fascinating natural phenomenon, and showcasing its potential in diverse optimization challenges. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a simple yet effective grid search method, resulting in robust performance across a range of test instances.

title: Capybara-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Capybara-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CIMA), motivated by the unique foraging behavior of capybaras. Capybaras are known for their efficient and adaptable foraging strategies in complex environments. CIMA leverages these characteristics to develop an optimization algorithm suitable for a wide range of problems. The algorithm incorporates a novel exploration strategy based on capybara's movement patterns and a modified constriction heuristic inspired by their resource selection. The performance of CIMA is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's key components include an adaptive population size, a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism, and a novel convergence criterion. The results show that CIMA effectively explores the search space and converges to optimal or near-optimal solutions in a reasonable time. The algorithm's design aims to balance exploration and exploitation, leading to robust performance across different problem types. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its application in more complex real-world scenarios.

title: Title: Emergent Topology in Constraint Optimization via Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of genetic algorithms to the challenge of constraint optimization, specifically focusing on the discovery of novel topological structures that can significantly enhance the performance of these problems. Traditional constraint optimization methods often rely on local search and simple heuristics, struggling to find optimal solutions across a broad space of possibilities. We propose a novel approach that leverages the power of genetic algorithms to explore a vast landscape of topology configurations, selecting the configurations exhibiting the highest performance benefits. This work demonstrates the potential of genetic algorithms to uncover topological features that are not readily apparent through conventional optimization techniques. The core mechanism involves a genetic algorithm designed to iteratively generate and evaluate topology configurations, prioritizing those that demonstrably improve objective function values. The resulting topology, while not explicitly defined, is expected to possess properties that facilitate efficient and robust constraint satisfaction.

title: 基于量子纠缠的图灵机优化
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement for optimizing the fundamental operation of a Turing machine. Traditional Turing machine optimization relies on classical algorithms and heuristics, often struggling with the inherent complexity of the search space. We propose a novel approach utilizing quantum entanglement to simulate the Turing machine's behavior, enabling a fundamentally different optimization paradigm. The core mechanism involves creating entangled qubits that represent the Turing machine's state, allowing for a more efficient exploration of the search space. This research demonstrates a preliminary framework for achieving significant improvements in the efficiency of Turing machine search.

title: Non-Linear Topological Geometry Probabilistic Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear topological geometry and probabilistic optimization to complex system optimization. We propose a novel approach that dynamically adjusts optimization parameters and structural elements based on probability distributions, ensuring algorithm consistency within complex environments. This method leverages the probabilistic properties of the optimization process to enhance efficiency and robustness. The core claim is that this approach offers superior performance compared to static optimization techniques by incorporating dynamic probability shifts. The research investigates the impact of this dynamic process on algorithm convergence and solution quality across diverse complex systems.

title: Emergent Logic Circuit Design
abstract: This paper explores the design of logic circuits through emergent principles, specifically leveraging self-organization and evolution to create circuits with complex functionality. The core idea is to move away from traditional, manually-designed circuits and instead utilize evolutionary algorithms to simulate the interactions between circuit components. This process harnesses emergent phenomena, leading to the spontaneous generation of novel circuit structures and functionalities. The approach avoids the limitations of conventional design methodologies, offering a potential pathway towards adaptive and self-optimizing circuits. This work focuses on the theoretical framework and underlying mechanisms, outlining a methodology for designing emergent logic circuits based on evolutionary strategies, without requiring experimental validation. The presented model introduces a new paradigm for circuit design, emphasizing the exploration of complex systems through simulated evolution. Key concepts include the representation of circuit components as genes in a genetic algorithm, the definition of fitness functions to guide the evolutionary process, and the evaluation of circuit performance based on emergent behaviors. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate the feasibility of designing circuits that exhibit complex logic directly through the principles of emergence.

title: Brown Lemur: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Brown Lemur Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Brown Lemur, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of brown lemurs. The algorithm leverages the lemur's strategy of systematically exploring and exploiting a territory, combined with their social dynamics and memory of previously visited locations, to achieve efficient optimization. Brown Lemur utilizes a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework with a new exploration and exploitation mechanism based on lemur territory mapping and social influence. The algorithm incorporates a "memory" component that mimics the lemur's recollection of favorable locations, and a "territory mapping" mechanism which guides exploration towards less-visited areas. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Brown Lemur through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Simulated Annealing (SA). The results indicate that Brown Lemur exhibits robust convergence properties and adaptability to diverse problem landscapes. The algorithm's core components are mathematically formalized, providing a clear and transparent description of its operational principles. Keywords: Metaheuristic, Particle Swarm Optimization, Brown Lemur, Optimization Algorithm, Territory Mapping, Memory, Social Influence.

title: Bronze Quoll: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bronze Quoll's Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bronze Quoll, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bronze Quoll ( *Setonix brachyurus* ), a small carnivorous marsupial native to Australia. The Bronze Quoll exhibits a unique strategy of prioritizing food sources based on a combination of proximity, estimated reward, and a degree of randomness. Bronze Quoll leverages these principles to create a novel optimization algorithm suitable for tackling complex, multi-objective problems. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a "Proximity-Based Exploration" phase, an "Estimated Reward Assessment" phase, and a "Randomized Search" phase, all dynamically adjusted based on problem characteristics. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and comparative analysis against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that Bronze Quoll performs competitively, particularly in scenarios where the problem landscape is characterized by diverse local optima and requires a balance between exploitation and exploration. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for a range of optimization applications.

title: 基于认知架构的程序设计语言
abstract: This paper proposes a novel programming language, termed "CogniLang," designed to directly mirror the concepts within cognitive architectures. The core claim is that by aligning programming syntax and semantics with cognitive models, we can significantly enhance program understandability, maintainability, and extensibility. The proposed approach involves constructing a compiler for CogniLang that translates source code into representations within a cognitive architecture, such as the Adaptive Control of Thought – Rational (ACT-R) system. This represents a fundamentally new paradigm by integrating cognitive science with programming language design. CogniLang aims to facilitate the creation of software that more closely reflects human cognitive processes, leading to more intuitive and robust applications. The paper outlines the key features of CogniLang, the proposed compilation process, and explores potential benefits and challenges of this approach.

title: Quantum-Inspired Adaptive Optimization for Deep Learning
abstract: Deep learning's remarkable success hinges on iterative optimization algorithms like stochastic gradient descent (SGD). However, training deep neural networks often encounters challenges navigating highly non-convex loss landscapes, frequently leading to convergence issues, slow training speeds, and susceptibility to getting trapped in local minima. This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, Quantum-Inspired Adaptive Optimization (QIAO), drawing inspiration from quantum measurement processes—specifically probabilistic sampling and collapse models—to address these limitations. QIAO employs a probabilistic strategy to sample regions of the loss landscape and utilizes a collapse model to iteratively refine the search, effectively mimicking the behavior of quantum measurement. The core idea is to leverage the inherent uncertainty and probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics to guide the optimization process more effectively than traditional gradient-based methods. We propose a framework for QIAO that incorporates adaptive step size adjustments and a dynamically adjusted sampling strategy. We demonstrate the efficacy of QIAO through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential through conceptual examples, highlighting its ability to adapt to complex loss landscapes. This approach aims to provide a fundamentally different strategy for deep learning optimization, potentially offering improved convergence rates and robustness compared to conventional methods.

title: Blue Duiker Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Blue Duiker Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the blue duiker ( *Cyanopica cooki*). BDMA combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) to create a robust and efficient algorithm for solving complex optimization problems. The core innovation lies in a dynamic adjustment of the exploration and exploitation phases, mimicking the duiker's adaptive movement strategy – a balance between searching for new food sources (exploration) and efficiently exploiting known good locations (exploitation). The algorithm utilizes a novel 'Duiker Velocity' concept, incorporating both a global and local search component, and a dynamic parameter adjustment scheme based on the estimated 'food availability' within the search space. The performance of BDMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results demonstrate that BDMA consistently outperforms or achieves comparable results with existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for various real-world applications.

title: Non-Linear Neural Networks: Adaptive Learning Strategies
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive learning strategies within non-linear neural networks to enhance model robustness and resilience to data noise and anomalies. Traditional neural network training often focuses on optimizing the model's parameters for the training data, neglecting the crucial role of dynamically adjusting learning strategies. We propose a novel architecture that incorporates a self-adaptive learning mechanism, adjusting network weights and biases based on the observed data's statistical characteristics. This approach aims to mitigate the impact of noise and outliers, leading to improved generalization performance. The paper details the design of this adaptive learning strategy, its implementation within a specific neural network framework, and presents preliminary experimental results demonstrating enhanced robustness to adversarial examples and data variability. The core claim is that this method significantly improves model performance compared to standard training techniques by incorporating adaptive learning.

title: ATTENTION-ENHANCED LSTM-BASED SOLAR POWER MANAGEMENT FORECASTING: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS WITH RECURRENT NEURAL NETWORK ARCHITECTURES
abstract: The prediction of solar power production plays an important role in the proper functioning and efficient management of renewable energy systems. Nevertheless, the solar power generation varies continuously with changes in weather conditions, which make the process of forecasting difficult. The purpose of this paper is to evaluate the accuracy of forecasting with the application of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) models combined with the attention mechanism for solar power prediction. The efficiency of the models is measured by means of the coefficient of determination (R²), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The research results show that the best results are obtained with the Attention + LSTM model, with the highest mean values of R² of 0.9555, MSE of 0.4205, and MAE value is 0.4521. title: Artificial Intelligence - Powered Project Management Tools for Enhanced Productivity: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming project management by enhancing productivity improving forecasting accuracy, supporting more informed managerial decision making. Despite the growing body of research on AI applications in project environments the literature remains fragmented across technological, managerial and organisational dimensions. This study addresses this gap through a concept-centric systematic literature review of peer-reviewed studies published between 2022 and 2026. Drawing on a final sample of 72 studies selected from an initial dataset of 205 publications, the review synthesises the literature into key thematic areas, namely AI-enabled productivity, predictive analytics, prescriptive analytics, AI-driven risk prediction, human–AI collaboration, ethical AI governance, digital ecosystems and data infrastructure, governance and organisational integration, sustainability, and managerial decision support. The findings indicate that AI has evolved from a supporting analytical tool into a strategic capability that enables proactive project management through early risk detection, real-time monitoring, performance optimisation, and intelligent decision support. The review further highlights that the effective adoption of AI depends not only on technological sophistication but also on organisational readiness, governance structures, data quality, and the integration of human judgement with intelligent systems. The study contributes to the literature by providing a structured conceptual synthesis of AI in project management and identifying important directions for future research particularly the need for integrated frameworks, empirical validation across the project lifecycle, and stronger attention to ethical and governance considerations in AI-enabled project environments.

title: Critical Raw Material Potential and Mineral System Architecture of the Northeastern Estonian Basement (Eastern Fennoscandia): Integration of Drill-Core Geochemistry, Geostatistics, and Geophysical Insights
abstract: Abstract Book of the conference (Pg, 108-109) https://iagod2026.inporto.events/docs/IAGOD_2026%20Abstract_Volume.pdf This presentation explores the concealed Precambrian basement of Estonia through an integrated geophysical and mineralogical approach. Gravity and magnetic data are used to characterize major lithological domains, structural boundaries, and subsurface bodies, supported by forward and inverse modelling and comparison with available geological and drill-core information. These regional-scale observations are complemented by high-resolution analytical techniques, including Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) for rapid geochemical and mineralogical characterization of drill-core material and FIB-TEM analyses for nanoscale investigation of selected mineral phases. By combining geophysical imaging with geochemical and microstructural observations across multiple spatial scales, the study aims to improve the interpretation of Estonia’s poorly exposed crystalline basement and to better constrain its geological evolution and potential for critical raw material mineralization

title: USB Subsystem Support for the Kirsch Project
abstract: The Universal Serial Bus (USB) is an easy to use, cheap and ubiquitous way of transferring data via a cable. With USB being indispensable for the modern computing world, it is only natural, wanting to utilize this standard for the Kirsch Project. The Kirsch Project tackles the problem that there are many processing units capable of general purpose computation and communication in modern computer systems, which is in conflict with the assumption traditional operating system make: that the application processing units, on which the operating system runs, are in control of the platform, while every other core is simply a peripheral. An assumption which fails to take into consideration that firmware, running on these other processing units, is often indistinguishable from a “proper” operating system. The Kirsch Project attempts to mitigate this problem by creating a collection of operating systems that are aware of the complex system on chip (SoC) environment they operate in and actually manage this infrastructure. This thesis designs a fine-grained compartmentalized, user space, USB subsystem and implements and evaluates it for the Cheriette operating system, which is part of the Kirsch Project. The implemented USB subsystem makes use of CHERI capabilities as well as Cheriette’s compartmentalization and secure call concepts in order to use isolation and the principle of least privilege to constitute a resilient subsystem with a minimal attack surface.

title: Thousands of Problems to Lean
abstract: Der interaktive Theorembeweiser Lean gewann in den letzten Jahren an Bedeutung. Ein prominentes Beispiel dafür ist die Verwendung von Lean von der mathematischen Gemeinschaft im Projekt zur Formalisierung der Mathematik in Mathlib. Ein attraktives Merkmal von Lean ist der kleine vertrauenswürdige Kern. Die Aufgabe des Kerns ist es, zu überprüfen, ob die formulierten Theoreme tatsächlich solche sind. Der Kern von Lean selbst ist nicht formal verifiziert, aber seine kleine Größe und seine klare Aufgabenstellung erzielen ein hohes Maß an Vertrauen in seine Korrektheit. Beweise in Lean zu schreiben kann sich als recht mühsam erweisen, weshalb es ein großes Anliegen ist, das Schreiben von Beweisen zu vereinfachen. Eine Methode, mit der es einfacher wird, Beweise zu schreiben, sind Automatisierungswerkzeuge, die für einfachere Theoreme vollautomatisch einen Beweis liefern können. Die „Thousands of Problems for Theorem Provers“ (TPTP, deutsch: Tausende Probleme für Theorembeweiser) Problembibliothek ist eine große Sammlung an Problemformulierungen, die in einem Format geschrieben ist, das von gängigen automatischen Theorembeweisern als Eingabe akzeptiert wird. Die Probleme der Bibliothek stammen aus verschiedenen Domänen und sind in unterschiedlichen Logiken und Theorien formuliert. Diese Bibliothek dient als Maßstab zur Evaluierung von automatischen Theorembeweisern. In dieser Arbeit stellen wir eine Übersetzung von Instanzen der TPTP-Problembibliothek nach Lean vor. Diese Übersetzung ist in zwei Lean Bibliotheken implementiert, die es ermöglicht, Instanzen die im TPTP-Format geschrieben wurden als Ausdrücke in Lean zu importieren. Durch diese Übersetzung steht die TPTP-Problembibliothek als Maßstab für Automatisierungswerkzeuge in Lean zur Verfügung. Wir nutzen diese Übersetzung um existierende Automatisierungswerkzeuge zu evaluieren. Wir analysieren die Leistungsfähigkeit unserer Werkzeuge indem wir sie mit der von Lean auf äquivalenten Eingaben vergleichen.

title: MODERN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE PLATFORMS IN BUSINESS
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of modern artificial intelligence platforms for business, with the aim of developing a structured classification of available tools and identifying the key factors that determine the success or failure of their implementation in corporate environments. The relevance of this topic stems from the growing gap between the widespread strategic commitment to AI and the limited practical results achieved by most organizations. Despite significant investments and high expectations, a large proportion of AI projects remain confined to pilot stages, failing to deliver tangible business value at scale. This disconnect highlights the absence of systematic approaches to navigating the fragmented landscape of AI solutions, which complicates decision-making and increases the risk of suboptimal technology choices. To address these challenges, the research employs a comprehensive methodological framework that integrates systemic analysis with comparative and classification methods. The study is based on a broad synthesis of empirical data, including global surveys of business leaders and IT professionals, as well as analytical assessments of platform capabilities. The classification criteria are defined around functional purpose, architectural flexibility, integration potential, and alignment with organizational maturity levels. This multidimensional approach enables a holistic view of the market and provides a foundation for identifying recurring patterns in both successful and failed implementations. The results of the study include a structured typology that distinguishes four major categories of AI platforms. The research also identifies critical success factors, including data integration quality, workforce competencies, governance frameworks, and measurable ROI systems, while simultaneously highlighting the phenomenon of AI regression, where organizations abandon previously adopted AI solutions due to unmet expectations, underscoring the importance of realistic planning and organizational readiness. The practical value of the research lies in its direct applicability to strategic and operational decision-making in technology management. The proposed classification and the identified success factors serve as a practical guide for selecting AI platforms that align with the specific needs and capabilities of an organization, helping reduce investment risks, avoid costly mistakes, and enhance the likelihood of successful scaling.

title: Rhino optimizer for hyperparameter tuning in depression detection
abstract: Depression detection using machine learning (ML) has gained increasing attention; however, model performance remains highly sensitive to hyperparameter configuration. This study introduces the Rhino optimizer, a novel bio-inspired metaheuristic algorithm for hyperparameter optimization (HPO) inspired by behavioral mechanisms observed in Rhinoceros movement and survival strategies. The optimizer integrates Lévy-flight exploration, elite-guided exploitation, wallowing-based escape behavior, and migration-based repositioning to balance exploration and exploitation while reducing premature convergence. The proposed approach was evaluated on a transformer-based depression-detection model using F1-score as the primary optimization objective due to the class imbalance commonly present in mental-health datasets. Performance was compared against traditional search methods, classical metaheuristics, and modern bio-inspired optimization algorithms under an identical evaluation budget. Rhino optimizer achieved a best observed F1-score of 0.8005, equivalent to the sine-cosine algorithm (SCA) and grey wolf optimization (GWO) with the same evaluation budget. Consistent convergence behavior and statistical analyses suggested that the proposed Rhino optimizer may serve as a competitive approach for HPO in depression detection and that behavior-inspired optimization strategies might be useful in machine-learning applications with limited computational resources.

title: Neural Network Simulation of Burner Operation Parameters
abstract: Abstract— The article presents the results of studying the applicability of deep learning methods for predicting the operation parameters of a liquid fuel fired burner with steam-assisted atomization and a gas generation chamber, which is intended for combusting low grade liquid hydrocarbon fuels and waste based on a flame visual analysis. The scientific novelty of the study is that with steam-assisted atomization it is possible to obtain visual flame patterns differing from those obtained using conventional methods, for interpreting of which a dedicated approach is required. A modified architecture of the dense convolutional neural network DenseNet-121 is proposed with weights pretrained on the ImageNet data set, which is adapted to solving the regression problem of predicting the device process operation parameters (fuel and superheated steam flowrates). The DenseNet-121 architectureс with dense interlayer connections is able to efficiently draw fine visual features from the flame images, which are critical for establishing the functional dependences. The regression subnetwork includes fully connected layers with the rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation and Dropout regularization. Validation on an independent test sample of experimental data has shown high accuracy of the model: for the fuel flowrate, the mean absolute error (MAE) is 3.8%; the root mean square error (RMSE) is 9%, and the determination coefficient R2 = 0.957; for steam flowrate the MAE is 2.6%; RMSE is 4%, and R2 = 0.994. The achieved results (R2 > 0.95 for both the parameters) confirm that the model is able to catch complex interrelations between the flame visual characteristics and burner operation parameters. The proposed solution is aimed at developing an intellectual tool for prompt contactless monitoring and optimization of liquid fuel combustion processes in burners with steam-assisted atomization and a gas generation chamber.

title: Digital pathology, image analysis, and artificial intelligence in liver disease
abstract: Advances in digital pathology, image analysis, and artificial intelligence (AI) are rapidly transforming how pathologists and researchers interact with tissue samples and enable the development of diagnostic tools that harness high-resolution whole-slide images; these advances are in turn creating new opportunities for research, education, and routine clinical care globally. Liver disease is no exception, and digital pathology and AI have many applications in the diagnosis of liver cancer and liver diseases and in the assessment and management of transplantation. Although quantitative image analysis techniques have been applied to liver disease in research settings for over 50 years, recent improvements in image resolution, data storage, and the availability of advanced AI methods such as deep learning have driven multiple exciting developments. In this Review, we summarise the advancements in digital pathology, image analysis, and AI in liver disease. Key challenges such as access to and the logistics of using digital solutions, quality issues, and appropriate guidance in research and clinical use are reviewed, along with potential solutions to these challenges in the context of liver pathology and liver disease. Digital technologies are well established in liver pathology research, and access in clinical practice is increasing, with potential to address current laboratory challenges. Further evaluation is required to assess real-world effectiveness, clinical safety, and implementation of AI tools in liver pathology.

title: Coordinated Suppression of Excess Noise for Continuous‐Variable Quantum Key Distribution in Unstable Channels Via Ensemble Learning
abstract: ABSTRACT Excess noise is a critical factor limiting the system performance of Continuous‐Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CVQKD). However, conventional suppression methods are optimized for a single type of excess noise and exhibit insufficient robustness in unstable channels, reducing the improvement of the secret key rate (SKR). Thus, this work proposes an ensemble learning‐based excess noise suppression framework. By fusing decision information from multiple submodels, ensemble learning frees the framework from the limitation of relying on a single excess noise distribution, enabling it to adapt to the characteristic differences of excess noise from diverse sources and ultimately achieve coordinated suppression of multi‐source excess noise. To further enhance the real‐time adaptability of the framework to unstable channels, the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) is introduced to optimize the hyperparameters of the ensemble learning model globally, ensuring the model can maintain stable suppression performance under changing channel environments. Experiments demonstrate that this scheme enables the centralized suppression of excess noise within the system, with a maximum suppression rate of 75%. The SKR is significantly improved by approximately 2.43 times, which verifies the effectiveness of the scheme in enhancing the system's performance.

title: UAV Thermal Imagery for Inert Ordnance Screening: Multi Campaign Dataset Development,Object Detection, and Practical Recommendations
abstract: Unexploded ordnance (UXO) continues to restrict civilian access, agricultural activity, infrastructure recovery, and environmental remediation in contaminated areas around the world. This study created a multi campaign UAV thermal image data set of inert ordnance, developed a labeled image set from collected imagery, tested object detection models, and identified practical considerations for humanitarian mine action and demining applications. Data were collected during four field campaigns in Tennessee under summer and winter conditions using inert mines, munitions, and other ordnance placed in short grass, tall vegetation, gravel, mulch, rock, compost, and compacted surfaces. Thermal imagery was collected under flight altitutes of 33 m and 15 m. The final source inventory contained 5,855 thermal image label pairs, including 918 positive images and 4,937 background images. After retaining all positive images and downsampling background images, the 33 m dataset contained 420 training and 106 validation images, while the 15 m dataset contained 629 training and 157 validation images. YOLOV11l and RT-DETR-R50 algorithms were trained and evaluated to develop an automated candidate detection model. Practical recommendations include collecting thermal and RGB imagery together, incorporating varied surfaces and background only imagery, considering periods following changes in solar exposure, balancing survey coverage against target pixel representation, calibrating models with representative local data, and retaining qualified human review. The intended use is screening and prioritization for follow on technical survey or EOD assessment, and not a standalone clearance.

title: Accurate Reconstruction of Gas Turbine Blade Geometry Using 3D/2D Rigid Registration and CT View Optimization
abstract: Non-destructive X-ray and computed tomography (CT) testing are essential for ensuring the dimensional accuracy of manufactured components with complex internal structures, such as the cooling channels in gas turbine blades, which directly affect thermal performance and service life. This study presents a multipart 3D-2D rigid registration approach for aligning CAD models with X-ray projections as an alternative to CT reconstruction for part inspection and measurement. A greedy registration algorithm sequentially aligns the blade's exterior before registering its internal components by maximizing the mutual information between simulated and acquired X-ray images. This stepwise approach reduces problem complexity and improves alignment accuracy. View angles are optimized using a greedy method that iteratively selects angles to minimize dimensional measurement errors. The results indicate that a small number of oblique views provides the best accuracy, although a broad range of angles yields acceptable results. The method achieves subpixel registration accuracy, with errors below one-fifth of the magnified detector-pixel pitch. Image noise and defects reduce registration precision, but direct registration in projection space mitigates these effects compared with CT reconstruction. Appropriate view selection can therefore preserve acceptable subpixel accuracy in the presence of image noise and defects.

title: Hints Help But Do They Teach? Evaluating Skills Transfer in Code Generation
abstract: When a hint turns a failing generated program into a passing one, does it provide missing information or merely steer the model toward a solution it could already produce? We test these hypotheses on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ using executable evaluation. For Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, adaptive relevant hints rescue 36 of 79 selected failures; an unrelated hint rescues 19, while eight unhinted samples solve 46 and recover 31 of the 36 relevant-hint rescues. Phi-3.5-mini shows the same pattern: relevant hints rescue 42 of 101 failures, an unrelated hint rescues 17, and unhinted sampling solves 57, including 36 of the 42 relevant-hint rescues. Because the hint conditions use different attempt budgets, these comparisons do not isolate a purely semantic effect. Mechanistic tests on Qwen identify a stable activation direction shared by relevant and unrelated hints. Persistently adding this direction yields 14 rescues and 18 regressions, with no detectable net accuracy gain; learned low-rank interventions have a positive but imprecise estimated effect. Full textual specifications solve 22 of 24 context-defined problems, versus 5-11 for tested virtual-KV prefixes. Post-generation hidden-state probes transfer across benchmarks, with pooled AUROC 0.806 and 0.780, but their top-one selection advantage over token confidence is statistically unresolved. Overall, relevant hints can rescue failures, but most rescued solutions are already reachable through ordinary sampling, and the internal interventions tested here do not establish task-general capability transfer.

title: Reinforcement Learning Enhanced LLM Agents for Complex Vehicle Routing Problems
abstract: Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs) are fundamental combinatorial optimization problems with widespread applications in various scenarios. The advanced optimization solvers can effectively solve such problems. However, modeling complex VRP variants for solvers often requires substantial domain expertise, which limits the accessibility of advanced optimization technologies. In this paper, we propose Reinforcement Learning Enhanced LLMAgents(RLEA), a multi-agent framework designed to automate the modeling of complex VRPs. RLEA introduces a lightweight neural Planner trained with Soft Q-learning to efficiently orchestrate the actions of LLM-based agents. In addition, we equip the system with an evolutionary memory module and retrieval-augmented generation, enabling the agent to leverage both accumulated experience and external solver knowledge during program generation and refinement for solving VRPs. We evaluated 48 distinct VRP variants across various solvers. The experimental results demonstrate that RLEA outperforms the previous state-of-the-ar method, achieving a 16.67% higher success rate while significantly reducing runtime errors. These results validate that integrating reinforcement learning with LLM-based reasoning is highly effective for automated optimization modeling. The appendix is available at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19134435.

title: TelcoAgent-Bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Telecom AI Agents
abstract: The integration of large language model (LLM) agents into telecom networks introduces new challenges, related to intent recognition, tool execution, and resolution generation, while taking into consideration different operational constraints. In this paper, we introduce TelcoAgent-Bench and TelcoAgent-Metrics, a Telecom-specific benchmarking framework for evaluating multilingual telecom LLM agents. The proposed framework assesses the semantic understanding as well as process-level alignment with structured troubleshooting flows and stability across repeated scenario variations. Our contribution includes a structured suite of metrics that assess intent recognition, ordered tool execution, resolution correctness, and stability across scenario variations, with the aim of quantifying the reliability and operational consistency of LLM agents in telecom environments. The framework is designed to operate in both English and Arabic, to address the need for multilingual agent deployment in operational network environments. Our experimental results show that although recent instruct-tuned models can understand telecom problems in a reasonable way, they usually struggle to consistently follow the required troubleshooting steps and to maintain stable behavior when exposed to different variations of the same scenario. This performance gap becomes more pronounced in unconstrained and bilingual settings.

title: Escaping Reasoning Basin Collapse with History-Biased Search
abstract: Inference-time search with large language models (LLMs) often concentrates on a small set of structurally or semantically similar trajectories, leaving alternative reasoning strategies underexplored---a failure mode we call \textit{reasoning basin collapse}. We introduce \textsc{BASIN}, a training-free, history-biased search method that groups reasoning states into basins and accumulates a revisit penalty on repeatedly selected basins, reallocating a fixed inference budget toward underexplored reasoning strategies. Under matched inference budgets, \textsc{BASIN} improves over Tree of Thoughts (ToT) by up to $+22$pp on Game of 24 and $+6.7$pp on MuSR. Because indiscriminate diversification can over-explore once search has found a promising basin, we further introduce \textsc{QA-BASIN}, a quality-aware variant that weakens the revisit penalty for high-quality basins and yields more robust gains. To characterize when basin-aware search helps, we introduce the \emph{redundancy gap} $Δ$, which measures the difference in search concentration between correct and incorrect predictions: standard ToT often operates near $Δ\approx 0$, whereas \textsc{BASIN} consistently shifts $Δ$ positive. Together, these results identify reasoning basin collapse as a failure mode of inference-time search and show that history-dependent bias provides a simple, training-free mechanism for escaping redundant reasoning under fixed compute. Code is available at https://github.com/GitHubLuCheng/basin
