title: Neural Symbollic Regression Using Deep Learning and Sparse Modelling
abstract: Symbolic Regression (SR) seeks to find succinct mathematical expressions that represent the fundamental relationships within data, providing interpretability and scientific understanding that exceeds that of black-box models. Nevertheless, traditional methods like Genetic Programming face challenges with scalability and are highly sensitive to noise, while sparse regression techniques such as SINDy rely significantly on predetermined feature libraries. In this work, we present a Neural Symbolic Regression (NSR) framework that treats neural networks as functional preconditioners for symbolic discovery. Our approach uses a decoupled pipeline: a neural network first learns a smooth, noise-robust approximation of the target function in an interaction- aware nonlinear feature space. LASSO is then applied to extract sparse, interpretable closed-form expressions. To improve predictive accuracy and symbolic fidelity by integrating distributed hyperparameter optimization with Ray Tune and ASHA scheduling. Experiments on the Nguyen benchmark suite show that our approach consistently outperforms SINDy and non-tuned neural baselines in RMSE, noise robustness, and out-of-distribution generalization. Ablation studies confirm the significance of feature interactions, neural depth, and tuning strategies. In general, this study presents a scalable and understandable neural-symbolic framework, creating a solid link between neural approximation and the discovery of sparse equations for scientific machine learning.

title: REVISE: Validity-Guided Recovery for Online Revisions in Agent Workflows
abstract: Agent revisions expose a fundamental correctness--efficiency trade-off during concurrent execution. Discarding ongoing work preserves latest-version correctness but wastes progress that may remain valid, whereas reusing prior work preserves efficiency but risks propagating stale state into outputs and tool effects. Existing recovery strategies resolve this trade-off in an imbalanced way with coarse-grained policies: they either favor efficiency by allowing potentially stale work to continue, or favor correctness by restarting the workflow or recomputing a linear suffix from the earliest conflict, thereby discarding unaffected progress. We present \textsc{Revise}, a validity-guided runtime for fine-grained recovery in structured agent workflows. When a revision arrives, \textsc{Revise} first intersects its delta with recorded data and control dependencies and propagates the resulting impact through the partially executed DAG to identify affected work. It then stops invalid work, preserves validity-established progress beyond the earliest conflict, and recomputes only the affected region. Incomplete provenance conservatively expands recovery, while reused results are revalidated before commit. Analysis of real coding-agent traces show online recovery opportunities: 118 sessions retain observable work before a queued later message is delivered; across 167 overlapping assistant responses, enqueue-to-completion overlap reaches 56.55~s at p95. Across 300 challenging revision/commit executions, \textsc{Revise} matches a latest-version oracle with no stale outputs or effects. On unmodified LangGraph and LLMCompiler applications using Qwen3-14B, it reduces model calls by 40.6--56.0\% relative to full restart and by 31.3--43.6\% relative to suffix recomputation. Under serving pressure, it further reduces revision-to-correct-completion tokens by 13.26\% and improves SLO goodput by 3.07--5.43\%.

title: Nested atoms model with application to clustering big population-scale single-cell data
abstract: We consider the problem of clustering nested or hierarchical data, where observations are grouped and there are both group-level and observation-level variables. In our motivating OneK1K dataset, observations consist of single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from 982 individuals (groups), totaling 1.27 million cells (observations), along with individual-specific genotype data. This type of data would enable the identification of cell types and the investigation of how genetic variations among individuals influence differences in cell-type profiles. Our goal, therefore, is to jointly cluster cells and individuals to capture the heterogeneity across both levels using cell-specific gene expressions as well as individual-specific genotypes. However, existing grouped clustering methods do not incorporate group-level variables, thereby limiting their ability to capture the heterogeneity of genotypes in our motivating application. To address this, we propose the nested atoms model (NAM), a new Bayesian nonparametric approach that enables the desired two-layered clustering, accounting for both group-level and observation-level variables. To scale NAM for high-dimensional data, we develop a fast variational Bayesian inference algorithm. Simulations show that NAM outperforms existing methods that ignore group-level variables. Applied to the OneK1K dataset, NAM identifies clusters of genetically similar individuals with homogeneous cell-type profiles. The resulting cell clusters align with known immune cell types based on differential gene expression, underscoring the ability of NAM to capture nested heterogeneity and provide biologically meaningful insights.

title: Verdict Instability of OOD Scores under Reference Resampling
abstract: Post-hoc out-of-distribution detectors are fitted on a finite reference set, so every score they produce is an estimate. If we had chosen a different set, some verdicts would have moved. We measure that movement by resampling the reference set and recording the bootstrap standard deviation of the score, which we call verdict instability. It admits a closed form with no fitted parameters. The instability of a verdict is the within-class dispersion of the assigned class along the query's direction, divided by the square root of that class's reference count. That count is what separates verdict instability from the geometry of the score distribution, and it is identifiable only under class imbalance. Instability grows with the local dispersion. Far-OOD queries lie along the low-variance directions of an anisotropic embedding, so every distance-based score we test assigns its highest values to the verdicts that are most reproducible. Only estimators of local dispersion carry the sign a practitioner expects. We give a rule that predicts this sign for any score from a single label-free correlation, and abstention driven by a wrong-signed score turns out worse than abstention at random on every dataset we test.

title: Edge-Girth as a Structural Edge Feature for Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNN) based on message passing are provably no more powerful than the one-dimensional Weisfeiler--Leman colour-refinement test (1-WL): two graphs it cannot tell apart receive identical representations, however deep or wide the network. A common remedy augments node or edge features with precomputed structural descriptors, most often counts of a fixed small subgraph such as triangles or longer cycles, but such counts require committing in advance to the size of the substructure counted, a choice usually made blind to the data. We study a descriptor that avoids this choice. The edge-girth of an edge is the length of a shortest cycle through it, and its multiplicity is the number of such shortest cycles; together they form a per-edge invariant that reports cycles of arbitrary length, computable exactly by a single breadth-first search per edge. Injected into a gated message-passing architecture, EGAGNN, it reaches a test MAE a factor three below the closest gated comparator on the ZINC-12k regression benchmark at 104k parameters; against bounded cycle-counting descriptors under the same architecture, it matches only a dictionary counting cycles up to length eight, using twice as many channels, while a dictionary capped at length four performs no better than no structural information at all. On graph discrimination we prove a matching limitation: on graphs where every edge sees the same number of shortest cycles of the same length, the descriptor becomes constant and any model built on it collapses back to the 1-WL bound. This holds without exception across all 400 pairs of the BREC benchmark: not one of the 90 such pairs is distinguished.

title: On the Reliability of Generative Augmentation: A Wasserstein-Based Theoretical and Empirical Study
abstract: Generative data augmentation is widely used to mitigate class imbalance, yet its theoretical effect on downstream generalization remains poorly understood. In this work, we develop a statistical framework for conditional generative augmentation and analyze its impact on classification risk. We formalize augmentation as a distribution-mixing process and show that the resulting risk distortion is controlled by both the augmentation strength and the class-conditional Wasserstein discrepancy between real and generated distributions. We further derive a capacity-dependent generalization bound based on Rademacher complexity, revealing an explicit trade-off between hypothesis complexity, augmentation intensity, and generative fidelity. Empirically, we evaluate the framework on binary and multiclass imbalanced classification tasks using Conditional GAN and Conditional WGAN-GP augmentation. Across datasets, CWGAN-GP consistently achieves lower Wasserstein discrepancies than CGAN, indicating improved distributional fidelity. However, improved fidelity does not necessarily translate into superior classification performance, with classical oversampling methods often remaining competitive. These findings support the central theoretical prediction that augmentation reliability is governed by distributional approximation error rather than predictive performance alone. Overall, this work establishes generative augmentation as a distributional perturbation process whose reliability can be quantified through Wasserstein-based measures and supported by finite-sample generalization guarantees. The proposed framework provides a principled foundation for evaluating synthetic data quality beyond classification accuracy alone.

title: A framework for rigorous evaluation of model-agnostic explainability methods: multi-metric statistical benchmarking, operational protocol, and reproducibility
abstract: Evaluating explainability methods requires more than a single faithfulness proxy. We present a modular benchmarking framework centered on quantitative XAI quality metrics: fidelity, stability, sparsity, computational cost, and faithfulness gap, plus an explicit method for operating the framework end-to-end. On the UCI Adult benchmark, we use a staged evidence protocol: a calibration/reproducibility stage (EXP1) followed by a primary com-parative/robustness benchmark (EXP2); the current merged recovery snapshot contains 299 committed result artifacts (99.7% artifact coverage) plus a 30-row SHAP recovery batch, yielding 275 analyzable unique runs out of 300 planned cells (91.7%). Across complete model-size blocks (5 models, N ∈ {50, 100, 200}), Friedman tests indicate significant method differences for fidelity (χ2 = 42.12, p = 3.78 × 10−9), stability (χ2 = 40.68, p = 7.65 × 10−9), sparsity (χ2 = 35.64, p = 8.92 × 10−8), faithfulness gap (χ2 = 45.00, p = 9.25 × 10−10), and runtime (χ2 = 30.44, p = 1.12 × 10−6). SHAP leads on fidelity/stability, DiCE leads on sparsity, and LIME remains fastest overall. We release the framework, operation protocol, and artifacts with explicit data-quality caveats for reproducible benchmark use under a quantitative-only claim scope.

title: Hamiltonian Learning through Lie-Theoretic Methods
abstract: This paper presents a method for identifying unknown coefficients of basis elements in an effective Hamiltonian of single-qubit cases.This is done directly from the measurement statistics of a quantum system's unitary evolution, utilizing a unique method of Lie algebra coefficient recovery.The method exploits the fact that repeated application of a unitary operator amplifies the generator coefficient linearly in the exponent.The result produces measurement probabilities that constrain the unknown coefficient differently at each power tested.Inversion of any single measurement probability yields a multivalued set of candidates due to the periodic nature of the trigonometric functions involved.However, the true coefficient can be identified as the unique true value satisfying a consistency criterion across all powers simultaneously.The method is demonstrated numerically for the single-generator Hamiltonian and extended analytically to the two-generator case where geometric (𝐻 𝑒 = 𝑎𝑋) (𝐻 𝑒 = 𝑎𝑋 + 𝑏𝑍), conjugation reduces the Hamiltonian to an effective single-generator form.Numerical simulations further verify the geometric reduction and the subsequent coefficient reconstruction for representative two-generator Hamiltonians, given a known rotation angle.In both cases, the correct coefficients are recovered from measurement statistics, without ancilla qubits, coherent control circuits, or prior knowledge of the system's spectrum; for the two-generator case, the rotation angle used to align the Hamiltonian is currently taken as given rather than estimated from data.

title: Development of a Biomechanical Analysis Prototype for Sports Dance Pedagogy Using Wearable Devices and Mobile Terminals
abstract: With the increasing demand for precision and personalization in physical education, biomechanics has emerged as a pivotal discipline in enhancing the quality of sports dance instruction. This study investigates the integration of biomechanical analysis and intelligent mobile terminals into sports dance pedagogy. It first proposes a system architecture that leverages wearable devices and multimedia teaching terminals to enable real-time feedback, kinematic analysis, and personalized instructional support. Based on national curriculum standards and pedagogical theory, a hierarchical indicator system comprising 3 primary, 10 secondary, and 32 tertiary teaching strategy indicators was constructed and validated using expert consultation and Kendall’s concordance test (W > 0.75). A weighting system was then applied to rank the importance of each indicator. A case study involving 25 physical dance instructors across six universities was conducted to evaluate current teaching practices and assess the applicability of the proposed strategy framework. Results indicate that most instructors rely heavily on traditional methods such as demonstration and verbal instruction, with limited use of multimedia or theoretical integration.

title: Real-Time Credit Card Fraud Detection Using Machine Learning: Design, Evaluation and Deployment of an Interactive Fraud Detection System
abstract: Abstract Credit card fraud detection presents a significant machine-learning challenge because fraudulent transactions typically represent only a small proportion of financial activity. This study presents the design, development, evaluation and deployment of a machine-learning system for detecting potentially fraudulent credit card transactions. The study uses a dataset containing 339,607 transactions, including 1,782 fraudulent transactions (0.52%), representing a highly imbalanced binary classification problem. An end-to-end machine-learning pipeline was developed incorporating exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, categorical encoding, stratified train-test splitting, class-imbalance treatment using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), comparative model training and performance evaluation. Four supervised machine-learning algorithms were evaluated: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and XGBoost. Performance was assessed using AUC-ROC, Precision-Recall AUC (PR-AUC), precision, recall and F1-score, rather than relying solely on classification accuracy. XGBoost achieved the strongest overall performance, with an AUC-ROC of 0.9956 and PR-AUC of 0.8633. At the standard 0.50 classification threshold, the model achieved 89.33% recall, 43.80% precision and an F1-score of 58.78%. Decision-threshold optimisation was subsequently performed to investigate the trade-off between precision and recall. At an optimised threshold of 0.95, XGBoost achieved 91.03% precision, 74.16% recall and an F1-score of 81.73%, demonstrating a substantial improvement in the balance between precision and recall for the evaluated dataset. The selected XGBoost model was integrated into an interactive Streamlit application providing exploratory data analysis, model comparison, ROC and precision-recall visualisation, confusion matrices, feature-importance analysis, threshold optimisation and transaction-level fraud probability prediction. The study demonstrates an end-to-end application of artificial intelligence and machine learning to financial fraud detection, combining data preprocessing, imbalance handling, predictive modelling, model evaluation, threshold optimisation and interactive deployment.

title: Title: Auto-Generated Temporal Logic for Agent Behavior Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the application of auto-generated temporal logic (ATL) for agent behavior modeling. The core challenge lies in automatically creating temporal logic rules that accurately represent and predict complex decision-making processes within an agent system. We propose a novel reinforcement learning framework that iteratively refines temporal logic rules based on observed system dynamics, enhancing the system's predictive capabilities. This approach tackles the limitations of traditional rule-based modeling by allowing for dynamic adaptation and improved robustness. The research demonstrates the efficacy of this method through a series of simulations focusing on scenarios involving strategic decision-making and adaptive behavior. The findings highlight the potential of this technology to advance the field of agent-based modeling and predictive analytics.

title: 基于量子退相干的分布式计算架构
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computing architecture leveraging the phenomenon of quantum decoherence for efficient parallel computation. The core idea is to decompose computational tasks into smaller units and distribute them across multiple quantum nodes. Quantum entanglement is utilized to facilitate coordinated computations between these nodes. Unlike traditional distributed computing approaches, this architecture harnesses the inherent properties of quantum mechanics, specifically decoherence, to achieve computational speedups. The architecture is designed to mitigate the challenges associated with quantum error correction and communication latency, offering a potentially scalable solution for complex quantum computations. The theoretical framework and key components of this architecture are outlined, demonstrating its feasibility and potential impact on the future of distributed quantum computing. We explore the fundamental principles, focusing on the manipulation of quantum states and the control of decoherence effects. The design emphasizes robustness and scalability, addressing critical aspects for practical implementation.

title: 基于自适应的概率场模型的计算效率优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing the computational efficiency of machine learning models, specifically focusing on probability field models. Traditional methods often employ static parameter adjustments, which can lead to suboptimal performance and overfitting. We introduce a dynamic adaptation mechanism that dynamically adjusts probability field parameters based on the observed training data, allowing the model to converge more quickly and achieve improved accuracy. The core of this optimization relies on a carefully constructed probability field that captures the inherent uncertainty in the data, enabling the model to better represent complex relationships. We detail the algorithm's implementation, provide a comprehensive analysis of its performance, and demonstrate its efficacy on several benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in computational efficiency and predictive accuracy compared to existing methods.

title: 自适应量子拓扑结构映射的计算
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, offers the potential for dramatically enhanced quantum computation. This paper introduces a novel computational framework, the "Adaptive Quantum Topology Mapping" (AQTM) algorithm, designed to automatically adjust quantum topology structures and facilitate complex transformations crucial for expanding quantum computing capabilities. The core of the AQTM algorithm lies in its adaptive mapping mechanism, which dynamically adjusts the topology of a quantum system based on predefined criteria and feedback, offering unprecedented control over the evolution of quantum states. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, including its key components, operational procedures, and initial experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in performing significant quantum transformations. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of this approach on the future of quantum information processing.

title: Core Claim: Exploring a topological structure-based approach for geometric tensors, designing a computation paradigm leveraging quantum computing acceleration, and proposing new quantum algorithms.
abstract: The study of geometric tensors and their topological properties has emerged as a significant area within advanced mathematics and physics, offering potential for novel computational paradigms. This paper investigates the application of topological structure-based methods to geometric tensors, aiming to design a quantum computing acceleration paradigm. Specifically, we explore a novel approach to represent and manipulate geometric tensors through a topological structure, and propose a new quantum algorithm predicated on this structure. The core mechanism centers on introducing a topological structure onto the tensor, allowing for efficient optimization and simulation. The potential for quantum acceleration stems from exploiting the inherent properties of topological spaces and the ability of quantum algorithms to explore complex geometric spaces. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and robust computational methods, and highlights the synergistic relationship between topological structures and quantum computation. Furthermore, we analyze the implications of this approach for various geometric manipulation tasks, including optimization problems and simulation of complex physical systems. The proposed quantum algorithm utilizes the topological structure to guide the computation, achieving significant speedups compared to classical methods. The work offers a novel perspective on utilizing topological structures to enhance quantum computing, with implications for diverse mathematical and physical applications. Ultimately, this paper presents a framework for constructing quantum algorithms that benefit significantly from the unique properties of geometric tensors, demonstrating the potential for quantum computation to surpass classical approaches in certain complex scenarios. This investigation focuses on the core mechanism of representing geometric tensors using topological structures, and explores how this structure can be leveraged to accelerate computations.

title: Bottlenose Dolphin-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bottlenose Dolphin-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDIMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of bottlenose dolphins. The algorithm mimics the dolphins' unique echolocation and cooperative hunting strategies to effectively navigate and optimize complex search spaces. BDIMA incorporates three key components: (1) an echolocation mechanism for local exploration, represented by a Gaussian function to generate candidate solutions; (2) a cooperative hunting strategy, implemented through a weighted average of neighboring solutions; and (3) a dynamic adjustment of the exploration-exploitation balance, mirroring the dolphins' adaptive behavior based on environmental feedback. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results demonstrate that BDIMA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising approach for tackling challenging optimization problems across various domains.

title: Bornean Woolly Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bornean Woolly Bat (BWB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of Bornean woolly bats. These bats exhibit a unique and remarkably efficient strategy for locating food sources in complex environments. The algorithm leverages this behavior by incorporating key aspects of their echolocation and search patterns into a stochastic optimization framework. Specifically, the BWB algorithm utilizes a population of bats, each represented by position and velocity vectors. The algorithm's core mechanisms mimic the bats' echolocation process through a probabilistic distance measurement and a dynamic adjustment of velocity based on the perceived food source location. The algorithm's parameters, including the exploration and exploitation balance, are dynamically adjusted based on the bats' collective behavior, aiming to improve convergence speed and solution quality. The effectiveness of the BWB algorithm is demonstrated through its application to several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results show that the BWB algorithm consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of convergence speed and solution accuracy. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to a wider range of complex optimization problems, including those encountered in engineering and scientific fields.

title: Hierarchical Temporal Difference Learning with Memory Consolidation
abstract: Temporal Difference (TD) learning has been a cornerstone of reinforcement learning, but its performance often degrades significantly when applied to complex, long-horizon tasks with sparse reward signals. Standard TD learning struggles to propagate information effectively over extended sequences, leading to slow learning and premature convergence to suboptimal policies. This paper introduces a novel approach, Hierarchical Temporal Difference (HTD) learning with Memory Consolidation, designed to address these limitations. We propose a hierarchical framework where sub-policies learn at lower levels, and a memory consolidation mechanism selectively transfers learned knowledge – both policies and value functions – to higher levels based on their demonstrated relevance and stability. This allows the system to focus computational resources on the most promising learned behaviors, significantly improving learning efficiency and enabling effective exploration in challenging environments. The core claim is that standard TD learning's struggles with long-horizon tasks and sparse rewards limit its applicability. The proposed mechanism, memory consolidation, offers a new approach to overcome these challenges. The paper details the key components of the HTD framework and demonstrates its effectiveness through conceptual analysis and theoretical considerations.

title: ## Bolivian Tuco-tuco: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of the Bolivian Tuco-tuco
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bolivian Tuco-tuco" (BT), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bolivian Tuco-tuco ( *Digalia exstecta* ). This animal is known for its unique and seemingly random movement patterns while searching for food in a patchy environment. BT leverages these characteristics to develop a new optimization strategy. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, mimicking the Tuco-tuco's ability to adapt its movement strategy based on the perceived availability of resources. Specifically, BT incorporates a 'patch preference' mechanism, where individuals evaluate the fitness of potential solutions based on their proximity to previously successful regions. This mechanism, coupled with a stochastic movement component, aims to enhance the algorithm's convergence speed and robustness. The performance of BT is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities and potential for application in diverse fields.

title: Too Simple, Too Complex, Just Right: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of deep learning and inductive bias as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Hierarchical Relational Reasoning with Dynamic Dependency Graphs
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to relational reasoning, addressing the limitations of existing systems in handling complex, multi-level relationships and dynamic dependencies. The proposed system leverages a hierarchical representation of relationships alongside a dynamically evolving dependency graph. This architecture enables efficient inference across multiple levels of abstraction by adapting to changes in the relational landscape. The core mechanism involves learning this hierarchical structure and updating the dependency graph based on observed interactions. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach to significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of relational reasoning tasks. The system's ability to learn and adapt represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a more nuanced and flexible solution compared to static relational models. The key contributions are the integration of hierarchical representation and dynamic dependency graphs, leading to enhanced reasoning performance. The system's architecture is designed for scalability and adaptability, making it suitable for diverse relational reasoning applications.

title: Authenticity, Trust, and AI Skepticism in Green Advertising: How AI and Human Endorsers Influence Purchase Intention in E-Commerce
abstract: Despite the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) endorsers in advertising, evidence of their effectiveness remains mixed. This study examines how AI and human endorsers influence purchase intention in green e-commerce advertising through the parallel and sequential roles of perceived authenticity and perceived trust. It also investigates whether AI skepticism moderates the relationship between endorser type and perceived authenticity. In a between-subjects experiment, 521 South Korean adults were randomly assigned to view a green advertisement featuring either a human or an AI endorser. The results indicate that endorser type did not directly affect purchase intention. Instead, its influence began with authenticity, which mediated the effect independently and also initiated a sequential pathway through trust. Trust therefore functioned only downstream of authenticity and did not independently mediate the relationship. AI skepticism moderated the effect of endorser type on authenticity, with the human endorser’s authenticity advantage narrowing as skepticism increased. The sequential indirect effect also weakened at higher levels of AI skepticism. These findings position endorser type as a source cue whose influence begins with authenticity judgments and may subsequently extend through trust. The study advances research on AI endorsers and green advertising by identifying the mechanisms and boundary conditions that underlie the effects of endorser type. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of substantiating environmental claims and testing AI and human endorsement strategies across relevant audience segments.

title: Toward a Culturally Embedded Arabic LLM: Localizing Linguistic AI for the Arab World
abstract: Arabic large language models (LLMs) increasingly support communication, education, public services, and knowledge access, yet fluent Arabic generation does not necessarily constitute culturally appropriate understanding. This paper examines the problem of cultural and pragmatic misalignment in contemporary Arabic-capable models and proposes a framework for culturally embedded Arabic AI. Cultural embeddedness is operationalized through four interrelated capacities: Arabic-native semantic representation, register awareness, cultural inference, and dialectal continuity. Using a mixed-methods design, the study introduces the Culturally Sensitive Test Suite for Arabic (CSTS-Arabic) and a four-dimensional Cultural Quotient (CQ-Score) for evaluating contextual appropriateness, dialectal consistency, cultural-reference integrity, and pragmatic success. The study compares multilingual models, Arabic-focused models, and a proof-of-concept Culturally Aware Language Model (CALM). The reported findings indicate a persistent cultural competence gap in multilingual systems and improved performance when dialect-aware representations, structured cultural retrieval, and pragmatic attention are integrated into the modeling pipeline. The paper further develops an Arabic-first architectural proposal, a tiered corpus strategy, and ethical safeguards concerning representation, doctrinal plurality, epistemic authority, evaluation bias, and resource justice. Rather than treating culture as an optional layer of factual knowledge, the study argues that it should be modeled as a constitute part of linguistic meaning. The proposed framework therefore positions culturally embedded Arabic LLMs as both a technical and governance challenge and offers a pathway toward more reliable, pluralistic, and regionally accountable Arabic AI.

title: The Influence of Voice Anthropomorphism in Generative AI–Based Short Video Content on Purchase Intention
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has transformed digital marketing through AI-generated voice-overs in short-form video content. However, empirical understanding of how voice anthropomorphism influences consumer behavior remains limited. This study investigates the impact of short video content characteristics and AI voice anthropomorphism on purchase intention, with cognitive trust as a mediating variable. A quantitative approach was employed, surveying 384 Indonesian social media users exposed to AI-generated voice content. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results indicate that content characteristics (usefulness, ease of use, entertainment) and all four anthropomorphism dimensions (appearance, behavioral, cognitive, emotional) significantly and positively influence cognitive trust and purchase intention. Emotional anthropomorphism emerged as the strongest predictor of cognitive trust. Cognitive trust significantly mediates the relationships between independent variables and purchase intention. These findings highlight the critical role of human-like vocal traits and rational trust evaluation in driving consumer purchase decisions, offering actionable insights for optimizing AI-driven marketing strategies in short-video ecosystems.

title: Mapping the Transformation of Retailing in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This paper aims to conduct a systematic literature review (SLR) of the area of artificial intelligence (AI) and retail focusing on consumer behaviour to find the main themes, theory and methodologies used in this fast-growing research field. After careful screening process involving the identification of 701 records from the SCOPUS database, the study was conducted. An eligibility criterion with regard to AI, retailing and consumer behaviour was applied to reach the final sample of 56 articles. The selection process was conducted following the guidelines of the PRISMA 2020, which included a systematic and transparent process. The review shows that AI research in retailing clusters around four recurring themes: (a) AI, retailing, and customer satisfaction; (b) AI, customer satisfaction, and repurchase intention; (c) online retailing and purchasing; and (d) order fulfilment, satisfaction, and loyalty. Quantitative designs dominate the field, the USA, India, and China are the leading contexts of study, and the literature draws on a fragmented set of behavioural theories rather than a unifying framework. The review is limited to Scopus-indexed, English-language journal articles published up to May 2024. Twelve future research questions (FRQs), each traceable to a specific evidence gap, are proposed to guide subsequent enquiry. This is among the first SLR-PRISMA studies to systematically map the AI-retailing-consumer behaviour literature into thematic clusters and to translate cluster-level tensions directly into a gap-to-question research agenda, offering a transparent and reproducible foundation for future work in this domain.

title: Balancing Explainability Strength and Privacy in Counterfactual Explanations for Insider Threat Detection
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) methods, such as counterfactual explanations, help make model decisions more transparent and actionable. However, they can unintentionally reveal sensitive information, which is a critical concern in security settings such as insider threat detection, where both transparency and privacy are vital, particularly when explanations are shared with external analysts or decision-makers. We propose a privacy-aware counterfactual framework that integrates Differential Privacy (DP) to add only the minimum adjusted noise required to satisfy user-defined privacy caps, reducing information leakage while preserving explanation fidelity. Two task-specific metrics are introduced: XAIStrength, which measures how faithfully a counterfactual follows the model’s decision boundary, and XAILeakage, which quantifies privacy risk based on movement into sparse feature regions. Experiments on the CERT insider threat dataset show that initially generated counterfactuals were highly faithful for most users but frequently violated privacy requirements. After optimisation, leakage was reduced to meet strict, moderate, and lenient privacy caps (τ = 0.05/0.10/0.20) while maintaining practical fidelity. More than 60% of users retained Sopt ≥ 0.70 under strict privacy constraints, while over 60% maintained Sopt ≥ 0.85 under moderate privacy settings. Comparative evaluation against standard and privacy-aware baselines shows that the proposed framework achieves a stronger balance between explanation utility and disclosure risk. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to formally quantify and optimise the XAIStrength–XAILeakage trade-off in counterfactual explanations using statistically grounded risk measures and DP-calibrated optimisation.

title: Dual-Use Quantum Technologies for Resilient Maritime Cybersecurity
abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of quantum technologies is reshaping the landscape of cybersecurity, communications, and critical infrastructure protection, including maritime logistics infrastructures, smart ports, vessel traffic management systems, and autonomous maritime platforms, while simultaneously generating both substantial opportunities and emerging security challenges. Emerging paradigms such as Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), quantum networks, and post-quantum cryptography challenge the adequacy of classical security mechanisms. This study aims to examine the dual-use nature of quantum technologies and evaluate their implications for secure communication and navigation systems in maritime logistics, smart port ecosystems, and defence-oriented environments. The research adopts a conceptual and analytical approach, examining current developments in quantum technologies along with their cybersecurity implications. It evaluates the limitations of existing cryptographic systems in the context of quantum computing advancements and explores hybrid security models that integrate post-quantum cryptography with quantum communication techniques. The analysis also considers defence-oriented requirements, including resilience, secure communications, and the protection of critical infrastructure within NATO-aligned environments. The findings highlight that classical cryptographic approaches are increasingly vulnerable to quantum-enabled attacks, necessitating a transition towards quantum-resilient architectures. The study identifies the strategic advantages of quantum technologies, such as enhanced security through QKD, while also highlighting associated risks, including implementation complexity, operational constraints, and policy challenges. The dual-use character of these technologies is shown to have significant implications in both the civilian and military sectors. Finally, the paper proposes a unified conceptual framework that bridges current cybersecurity practices with emerging quantum-enabled paradigms. The framework supports the development of adaptive, sustainable, and future-proof security architectures capable of addressing evolving threat landscapes. The results underscore the importance of coordinated technological, operational, and policy efforts to ensure secure adoption of quantum technologies in critical domains. Special attention is paid to the resilience of maritime communications and navigation infrastructures against quantum-enabled cyber threats, including GNSS spoofing, communication intercept, and supply-chain disruption.

title: SC-CP: spatially-correlated conformal prediction for GNN-based distributed photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Abstract High-penetration distributed photovoltaic (DPV) generation exposes distribution grids to rapid, spatially-coupled power swings under passing cloud fronts, so secure dispatch of reserves, storage, and voltage-control devices hinges on prediction intervals with trustworthy coverage , not point forecasts. Two limitations of current practice are particularly costly in this physical setting: graph neural network (GNN) forecasters reproduce inter-site spatial coupling but emit only point estimates, leaving operators without a quantified risk margin; classical conformal prediction (CP) restores a marginal coverage guarantee yet calibrates each site independently, so a single cloud passage that drives correlated errors across neighbouring DPV plants collapses the joint guarantee exactly when reserve and voltage margins are tightest. We propose Spatially-Correlated Conformal Prediction (SC-CP) , which reuses the adjacency matrix already learned by the GNN backbone to weight nonconformity scores by inter-site error coupling, so that meteorologically co-driven errors inflate the interval while isolated anomalies do not. As an integral component of SC-CP, a Site-Adaptive Coverage (SAC) rule reallocates the global miscoverage budget non-uniformly across feeders in proportion to their calibration difficulty. Experiments on five NREL stations in northern California confirm that SC-CP restores nominal coverage in spatially-correlated regimes where standard CP systematically undercovers, and a real heterogeneous validation on the four German TSO control zones from the Open Power System Data release shows that SC-CP reduces the per-zone PICP spread of Standard CP by roughly 40%, with SAC supplying the expected non-uniform per-zone budget on the harder zones.

title: CircuitsDNA: Discovering Unconventional Multi-Accuracy Arithmetic Circuits via Evolutionary Synthesis
abstract: Emerging edge AI workloads increasingly require arithmetic units that can trade computational accuracy for efficiency on demand. However, existing approximate arithmetic circuits are typically fixed-accuracy or rely on predefined structures for runtime configurability. This work introduces CircuitsDNA, an evolutionary framework that automatically evolves accuracy-configurable arithmetic circuits supporting multiple accuracy modes within a single circuit. It integrates three key features: 1) multi-threshold verifiability miter to enforce mode-specific accuracy requirements, 2) resource-limited verifiability-driven search to reduce verification overhead without sacrificing correctness, enabling efficient exploration of large circuit design, and 3) feedback-driven adaptive mutation to prioritize effective structural modifications and accelerate search convergence. Experimental results show that the 8-bit multiplier variants synthesized in 28-nm CMOS reduce the area-power product by up to 56% on INT8 DNN workload and 93% under exhaustive activity, compared with an exact 8-bit multiplier. Across CNNs and DeiTs, the accuracy loss relative to FP32 remains below 2% after fine-tuning under worst-case error (WCE) budgets of at most 1%. CircuitsDNA eliminates all search stalls observed in conventional methods across 8/12/16-bit multipliers, while adaptive mutation provides up to 1.33 times faster convergence than its non-adaptive counterpart.

title: Does Fault Localization Beat a Fresh Attempt? A Placebo-Controlled Study of Test-Guided Code Repair
abstract: Fault localization can focus a code model's repair on the statements a failing test implicates, but a targeted edit may succeed merely because it is small, and a second model call may succeed without using the failure at all. We separate these explanations with three arms applied to the same failed candidate: blind whole-solution resampling, spectrum-based localization followed by suspect-span infilling, and same-length infilling at a disjoint random code span. Across three frozen 26-32B models, three benchmarks and 488 failing candidates, plus a separately declared 24B fourth model from a third family, three results follow. First, localization is rarely available: only 9.0% of failing candidates expose a failing public test with a usable spectrum. Second, among the 177 candidates localizable from a strong suite, localized infilling loses decisively to blind resampling at a matched attempt count (3:40, p = 3.0 x 10^-9), opposite to our hypothesis; the loss replicates in a third family at -11.3 points (95% CI [-16.6, -6.8]), and widening the edit does not rescue it. Third, against the random-span placebo localized infilling leads pooled (11:1, Holm-adjusted p = .019), but that lead resolves in no individual model under the analysis our shipped plan designates primary (best Holm p = .087), so we report the location effect as suggestive rather than established. Re-pricing attempts as tokens narrows but does not overturn this: a span attempt spends 21.7 generated tokens against 371.1, yet 16 localized attempts reach 6.8% while one blind attempt already reaches 10.1%. Infilling reproduces the removed span verbatim in 48.9% of attempts, which is why more budget does not help. We restrict every localization conclusion to the 24-32B models tested.

title: INTARG: Informed Real-Time Adversarial Attack Generation for Time-Series Regression
abstract: Time-series forecasting aims to predict future values by modeling temporal dependencies in historical observations. It is a critical component of many real-world systems, where accurate forecasts improve operational efficiency and help mitigate uncertainty and risk. More recently, machine learning (ML), and especially deep learning (DL)-based models, have gained widespread adoption for time-series forecasting, but they remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. However, many state-of-the-art attack methods are not directly applicable in time-series settings, where storing complete historical data or performing attacks at every time step is often impractical. This paper proposes an adversarial attack framework for time-series forecasting under an online bounded-buffer setting, leveraging an informed and selective attack strategy. By selectively targeting time steps where the model exhibits high confidence and the expected prediction error is maximal, our framework produces fewer but substantially more effective attacks. Experiments show that our framework can increase the prediction error up to 2.42x, while performing attacks in fewer than 10% of time steps.

title: Rethinking noise in quantum machine learning: When noise improves learning
abstract: Quantum noise is conventionally viewed as a fundamental obstacle in near-term quantum computing, motivating extensive error correction and mitigation strategies. We present numerical evidence within an effective noise modeling framework that challenges this consensus. Through experiments on quantum graph neural networks for molecular property prediction, we observe heterogeneous, initialization-dependent responses within this effective noise modeling framework. Among randomly initialized models with identical architecture, approximately one-third show performance improvement under moderate noise, while a smaller fraction deteriorate and the remainder are marginally affected. We identify a strong negative correlation (r = −0.62) between baseline model performance and noise benefit, suggesting a regularization-like effect for under-optimized models while disrupting well-converged ones. The observed optimal noise level falls below theoretical predictions, indicating error cancellation in structured quantum circuits. These findings suggest that, within the adopted effective noise model, noise effects depend critically on initialization quality and need not be uniformly detrimental, motivating structure- and noise-aware optimization strategies.

We identify a strong negative correlation (r = -0.62) between baseline model performance and noise benefit, suggesting \REV{a regularization-like effect for under-optimized models while disrupting well-converged ones}. The observed optimal noise level falls below theoretical predictions, indicating error cancellation in structured quantum circuits. These findings suggest that, within the adopted effective noise model, noise effects depend critically on initialization quality and need not be uniformly detrimental, motivating structure- and noise-aware optimization strategies.

title: Does Imitation Learning Preserve Temporal Robustness in Dexterous Manipulation? An Expert-Learner Comparison Across Task Execution Speeds
abstract: Dexterous manipulation policies learned by imitation are typically evaluated for robustness to variation in scenes, objects, or instructions, but their performance across task execution speeds is less often examined. This leaves open how much temporal robustness a learner retains relative to the expert it imitates. We compare an expert and learner under the same task conditions, initial-condition draws, and speedup factors. We instantiate the evaluation in ParcelStow, a contact-rich task in which the robot acquires, reorients, and inserts a parcel. The demonstrations span the speedup range for the manipulation phases after parcel acquisition. A scripted expert and an Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy trained from the expert's demonstrations both achieve 100 percent task success at nominal speed. Their success rates diverge within the demonstrated range: at its maximum, expert success is 84 percent and ACT success is 53 percent. Two ACT policies with different parameter initializations show similar degradation, decreasing by 34 and 48 percentage points from nominal speed to the maximum demonstrated speed, compared with 16 points for the expert. Stage-level analysis shows that 35 of ACT's 47 failures at the maximum demonstrated speed are insertion misalignments. Under the relative-motion handoff, every ACT acquisition retains the parcel through reorientation and transfer in free space, but only 64 percent complete the overall task, compared with 95 percent after expert acquisition. Across all evaluated policies and speeds, none of the 414 acquisitions without force closure completes the task. Equal nominal task success therefore does not imply preservation of expert performance across execution speeds. Code, data, and evaluation scripts are available at https://github.com/coenwerem/parcelstow.

title: CATeye: Coupled Attribute-Topology Invariance Learning for Voucher Abuse Detection
abstract: Voucher abuse poses a major challenge in e-commerce, where malicious users exploit promotional vouchers for profit. Unfortunately, fraud patterns evolve rapidly over time and across regions, causing distribution shifts that degrade existing detection models unless retrained frequently. To tackle this, we propose the Coupled Attribute-Topology Invariance Learning framework (CATeye). The key challenge arises from coupled attribute-topology shift, where edges built from attribute proximity cause environment-driven attribute shift to induce shifted topology, thereby amplifying variant signals through GNN message passing. CATeye sees through such coupled shifts with two learnable selectors. First, an Attribute Invariance Selector (AIS) learns node-adaptive masks to filter out non-invariant attributes. Then, conditioned on retained invariant attributes, an Edge Invariance Selector (EIS) samples an invariant subgraph and isolates non-invariant edges. Using the resulting invariant and non-invariant components, CATeye constructs multiple views and applies view-specific objectives to emphasize domain-invariant representations while suppressing domain-specific variations. Experiments on both a proprietary dataset from Lazada, a major Southeast Asian e-commerce platform, and a public benchmark show that CATeye consistently outperforms nine strong domain generalization and graph anomaly detection baselines, achieving up to an 8.61% improvement in average F1 score over the strongest baseline. Source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Tian0426/CATeye.

title: Diffusion as a Training Curriculum for Timestep-Free Iterative Reasoning
abstract: Diffusion models and recursive reasoners are both iterative, but they carry information across iterations differently. We add a persistent hidden state to a diffusion denoiser and remove its timestep conditioning, leaving a single shared update that can be run to arbitrary depth. The result is an anytime solver: accuracy keeps improving with inference depth far beyond the rollout lengths and backpropagation window used in training, reaching 99.90% exact solve on Sudoku-Extreme. We also obtain 98.93% solve rate on Maze-Unique. Surprisingly, progressive denoising is unnecessary at inference: holding corruption at its maximum by replacing every non-clue variable with fresh Gaussian noise at each step retains near-perfect solving and converges to stable solutions. This simple noise-injection mechanism enables a single trajectory to efficiently explore the solution space and settle on the correct answer without parallel rollouts, candidate selection, or external verifiers required by prior reasoning models. Nonetheless, ordered annealed corruption remains critical during training, which suggests that diffusion's primary contribution to our anytime solver is not a sampling procedure at inference, but a denoising training curriculum.

title: Lung Tumor Detection and Localization System Using Faster RCNN Algorithm
abstract: Lung tumors represent a significant health challenge. Although, their early detection can improve patient outcomes, traditional diagnostic methods often fall short in accuracy and efficiency. Therefore, advanced algorithms are required to facilitate accurate and earlier tumor detection and localization. This study aims to enhance detection efficacy through a systematic methodology that includes image pre-processing, segmentation, feature extraction, classification, and localization. We have invested three CNN models; Our proposed CNN, VGG-16 and RESNET50 integrated with Faster R-CNN to detect and localize lung tumor in computed tomography images from the Iraq-Oncology Teaching Hospital/National Center for Cancer Diseases (IQ-OTH/NCCD) dataset. As a result, VGG-16 and RESNET50 attained detection accuracies of 97.66% and 97.20% respectively, while Our-CNN model achieved a detection accuracy of 97.20%, with an average test precision of 97.185 and an F1-score of 0.9737. For localization, ResNet50 and Our-CNN demonstrated accuracy based on Intersection over Union (IoU) at 89.47%, while VGG-16 achieved 73.68%.

title: Arnold's Bifurcation Principle Applied to Variational Quantum Optimization: Real-Time Hardware Prediction of Barren-Plateau Stalling
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms, such as the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), rely on classical optimization loops to iteratively update parameterized gate rotation angles. These algorithms frequently fail due to ``barren plateaus''---regions in the parameter space where the gradient field vanishes and optimization convergence permanently stalls. We show that a barren plateau is a classical fold or saddle-node bifurcation of the optimization parameter trajectory. We propose a proactive, full-stack mitigation framework consisting of an algorithmic compiler wrapper that continuously extracts the time-varying parameter vectors, converting them into a standardized, digitized bitstream. Henceforth, to achieve runtime stability, this digitized parameter manifold stream must be fed directly into a dedicated, co-located physical hardware controller implementing Arnold's Bifurcation Principle. The domain-blind hardware controller computes the parameter-flow Jacobian matrix in-register and tracks its leading eigenvalue. By measuring the phase-space velocity of the eigenvalue toward zero, the hardwired controller predicts the approaching barren plateau several clock cycles before it manifests, dropping an asynchronous interrupt line that commands the software wrapper to dynamically shunt the parameter updates onto a structurally stable alternative manifold branch.

title: Adaptive Meta-Learning for Hyperparameter Optimization via Simulated Annealing
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hyperparameter optimization that leverages adaptive meta-learning combined with simulated annealing. The core idea is to train a meta-learner to predict an effective annealing schedule for a given hyperparameter optimization problem. This schedule then dynamically guides a simulated annealing algorithm, enabling it to converge faster and more reliably. The method establishes a feedback loop where the optimization process itself informs the meta-learner's learning, creating a self-optimizing optimization system. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components of the system, highlighting its advantages over traditional hyperparameter optimization techniques. The effectiveness of the adaptive meta-learning approach is significantly enhanced by dynamically adjusting the exploration strategy based on the current state of the optimization. This paper provides a foundational framework for future research in adaptive and intelligent hyperparameter optimization.

title: FQ8 × WCM Quantum Reader
abstract: The parent paper [1] reduced the circuit synthesis of the optimal 24-outcome reader for the binarytetrahedral group 2T to a single fixed operator, the 2T group Fourier transform, and identified its dominantcost as FQ8, the 8×8 group Fourier transform of the quaternion group Q8. The companion addendum [2]reported, as an honest negative, that on the parent paper's generic Givens-based emitter astructurally-built FQ8 still costs 218-234 CNOT -- far above the O(101) structural estimate -- and framed thegap as a binary-embedding and generic-decomposition tax: an emitter artifact rather than arepresentation-theoretic obstruction. This note discharges that claim with verified circuits. Using only thestructure of FQ8 -- the plus/minus pairing induced by the center Z2 of Q8, which lets a single Hadamardseparate the character sector from the two-dimensional-representation sector -- we build an exactfactorization in which the sole entangling object is a single controlled two-qubit gate Cq2[Wr]. We thenshow that Wr has Cartan (KAK) coordinates (π/4, 0, 0), the CNOT class, so its two-qubit nonlocal core isone CNOT. Three constructions of FQ8 are emitted and verified equal to FQ8 up to global phase atmachine precision, giving a monotone progression of 234 → 33 → 23 emitted CNOT. Every number belowis a real emitted, verified circuit, not a cost-model estimate. We are explicit about what is not achieved: thesingle-digit floor implied by "one CNOT core" is not reached, because lifting Wr to its controlled form costsone Toffoli plus controlled-local flanks (14 CNOT as emitted); reducing this further is a compiler task, not anew representation-theoretic result. The result establishes that the 200-CNOT wall was largely an emitterartifact. ※ The license for codes is AGPL3.0-or-later

title: Catamarca Tuco-tuco: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Tuco-tuco in Catamarca, Argentina
abstract: This paper presents Catamarca Tuco-tuco, a new metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the observed foraging behavior of *Cavia sedentaria* (Tuco-tuco) in the Catamarca region of Argentina, specifically their movement patterns and resource selection strategies. Catamarca Tuco-tuco incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), utilizing a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism inspired by the tuco-tuco's ability to adjust its velocity based on terrain and resource availability. The algorithm employs a multi-dimensional search space represented by a swarm of particles, each with position (*xi*) and velocity (*vi*). The core innovation lies in the adaptive inertia weight calculation: *wi* = *w*0 + *φ* * ( *si* / || *si* || ) * ( *gbest* / || *gbest* || ) , where *w*0 is the initial inertia weight, *φ* is a random number between 0 and 1, *si* is the particle's current position vector, and || *si* || and || *gbest* || represent the magnitudes of the particle's and the global best position vectors, respectively. Furthermore, a probabilistic acceptance criterion, derived from the tuco-tuco's exploration-exploitation balance, is implemented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Simulated Annealing, Adaptive Inertia Weight, Tuco-tuco, Optimization.

title: Quantum Entanglement Spin Encoding for Cognitive Modeling
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cognitive modeling utilizing quantum entanglement and spin encoding. The core idea is that quantum entanglement, with its inherent parallelism and non-classical correlations, can provide a more accurate representation of complex cognitive processes compared to traditional classical models. We outline a framework where neuronal states are represented by quantum spins in superposition and interference, controlled through entanglement manipulation. This allows for the simulation of cognitive phenomena, such as decision-making, memory, and attention, by modulating the entanglement and interference patterns between spins. The potential for capturing previously inaccessible cognitive behaviors through this quantum approach is explored, suggesting a fundamental shift in how we model the human mind. The model is presented as a conceptual architecture and relies on theoretical formulations rather than experimental validation.

title: ## California Kangaroo Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Kangaroo Rat Metaheuristic Algorithm" (KRMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the California kangaroo rat (*Dipodomys calurus*). Kangaroos rats are renowned for their efficient and adaptive strategies in locating scarce food resources in complex, variable environments. KRMA leverages these observed behaviors – including exploration, exploitation, and dynamic adjustment of search parameters – to effectively solve complex optimization problems. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a set of candidate solutions (representing "rats") navigating a search space. Each rat's movement is governed by a novel probability distribution derived from the kangaroo rat's movement patterns, incorporating elements of random walks and targeted searching. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic adjustment mechanism for both the step size and the probability of moving towards the best solution, mimicking the kangaroo rat's ability to shift between exploration and exploitation. The performance of KRMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability and adaptability to diverse challenges. The core of KRMA lies in its adaptive parameter control, which dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance, a critical factor in the success of many metaheuristic algorithms. The results suggest that KRMA offers a promising alternative for tackling complex optimization problems, particularly those with non-convex landscapes and multiple local optima.

title: Brush-tailed Bettong Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bettong-Inspired Adaptive Search (BIAS)," inspired by the foraging behavior of the brush-tailed bettong, a small marsupial native to Australia. The bettong's unique strategy of alternating between exploratory and exploitative phases, combined with its efficient movement patterns, provides a strong foundation for algorithm design. BIAS leverages a dynamic population size, adaptive mutation rates, and a novel convergence criterion based on the bettong's movement velocity and distance travelled. The algorithm is designed to address complex optimization problems characterized by non-linearity, multi-modality, and discontinuities. The core of BIAS lies in a 'momentum-based exploration' mechanism that simulates the bettong's ability to maintain directional movement while adapting to local environmental changes. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, Sphere function, and a modified version of the Rosenbrock function. The results show that BIAS consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising tool for tackling a wide range of real-world optimization challenges.

title: ## Brazilian Arboreal Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Arboreal Mouse Algorithm (AMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian arboreal mouse (Maximyas nitedicus). This rodent's unique approach to navigating complex arboreal environments – utilizing a combination of random exploration and intelligent path selection – forms the core principle of the AMA. The algorithm employs a dynamic tree structure to represent the search space, mimicking the mouse's ability to establish and adapt its routes based on environmental factors. We detail the algorithm's design, including the encoding scheme, the tree construction process, the movement strategy, and the convergence criteria. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AMA through theoretical analysis and illustrate its performance with simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its potential for tackling complex, non-linear challenges. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as solution quality, computational cost, and convergence speed. The results demonstrate that AMA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, highlighting its suitability for diverse optimization scenarios.

title: Meta-Learning for Algorithmic Adaptation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of meta-learning techniques to achieve algorithmic adaptation, aiming to enhance learning efficiency. Traditional algorithms often require extensive tuning and optimization for specific tasks, leading to significant time and resource expenditure. Meta-learning, or "learning to learn," offers a promising solution by enabling algorithms to automatically adapt their parameters and structures based on experience gained from multiple related tasks. This research proposes a framework leveraging meta-learning to dynamically adjust algorithmic configurations, resulting in improved learning performance. We explore the core claim that utilizing meta-learning facilitates algorithmic adaptation and the underlying mechanism of learning how to learn. The novelty lies in the direct application of meta-learning to optimize algorithmic behavior, rather than focusing solely on the learning process itself. The presented methodology demonstrates the potential for substantial gains in learning efficiency across a range of problems. ---

title: Non-Local Graph Embedding for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph embedding technique, termed "Contextualized Graph Embedding Network" (CGE-Net), designed to enhance machine learning model performance by capturing complex relationships across multiple nodes and edges. The core mechanism involves utilizing a variational autoencoder to learn a latent space representation of the graph, enabling the incorporation of contextual information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CGE-Net through extensive experimentation on various graph datasets, showcasing improved accuracy and robustness in tasks such as node classification, graph classification, and link prediction. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design and implementation, highlighting its advantages over existing methods.

title: Adaptive Neural Architecture Search with Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural architecture search (NAS) that leverages the strengths of evolutionary algorithms and reinforcement learning. The core idea is to treat NAS as a sequential decision-making problem, where an evolutionary algorithm dynamically adapts the architecture of neural networks during the search process. A population of network architectures is maintained, and a reinforcement learning agent learns to adjust architectural parameters based on the network's performance, optimizing for a defined fitness function. This adaptive approach demonstrates improved efficiency and effectiveness compared to traditional, static NAS methods. The key contribution lies in the dynamic adjustment of the search space itself, guided by the reinforcement learning agent's understanding of the network's performance landscape. The resultant architectures exhibit superior performance across a range of tasks.

title: Geometric Quantum Simulation Algorithm Improvements
abstract: Geometric Quantum Simulation (GQS) is a novel quantum simulation technique that leverages the unique properties of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum entanglement and superposition, to significantly accelerate the simulation of complex geometric systems. This paper presents an improved GQS algorithm designed to overcome the computational bottlenecks inherent in traditional methods, offering substantial improvements in simulation speed and accuracy for a range of geometric models. The core of the algorithm centers around a refined quantum state preparation strategy, incorporating entanglement manipulation to reduce the number of necessary quantum gates, and a novel optimization loop to enhance the fidelity of the resulting quantum states. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this improved approach through rigorous analysis and comparison with established quantum simulation methods, showcasing its potential to revolutionize the simulation of intricate geometric phenomena. This work contributes significantly to the advancement of quantum computing by providing a practical and efficient method for tackling computationally demanding geometric simulations.

title: EVALUATION OF TEXT CLASSIFICATION ALGORITHMS: A STUDY ON CLASS IMBALANCE AND PREPROCESSING
abstract: This paper presents a controlled comparative study of traditional machine learning algorithms for thematic text classification, focusing on the impact of preprocessing strategies and class imbalance on model performance under different data conditions. Two experimental scenarios were considered: the Women’s Clothing E-Commerce Reviews dataset, characterized by a highly imbalanced class distribution, and the AG News dataset, used as a balanced reference dataset. The preprocessing pipeline included text cleaning, stopword removal, tokenization, lemmatization, TF-IDF vectorization, class balancing, and dimensionality reduction. Six models were evaluated: Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, and K-Means as an unsupervised baseline. The results show that Random Forest achieved the best performance on the imbalanced Clothing dataset, reaching an accuracy of 0.763, an F1-score of 0.777, and an MCC of 0.739. In contrast, K-Nearest Neighbors obtained the highest scores on the balanced AG News dataset, with an accuracy and F1-score of 0.927. Naive Bayes showed limitations when dealing with sparse and ambiguous textual representations. The main contribution of this work is a systematic experimental analysis that highlights how preprocessing decisions, feature sparsity, and class distribution influence the behavior of traditional machine learning models in text classification tasks. These findings provide useful insights for model selection and evaluation under different data scenarios. Key Words: Text Classification; Text Preprocessing; Machine Learning; Text Analysis; Class Imbalance

title: DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING CONTROL OF A TENSION-CONSTRAINED TENDON-DRIVEN UNDERACTUATED ROBOTIC FINGER: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF DDPG AND SAC
abstract: Tendon-driven robotic fingers are underactuated and strongly nonlinear, and their unidirectional, friction-attenuated tendon tension imposes actuation constraints that any practical controller must respect. A previous study established that a deterministic learning controller (DDPG) can track a grasp trajectory for such a finger and compared it against model-based schemes. The present work extends that line of investigation by asking a narrower but unresolved question: for this same single-actuator, three-link tendon-driven architecture, how does a deterministic actor-critic policy (DDPG) compare with a stochastic, maximum-entropy policy (SAC) once a tension-limit penalty is built directly into the learning objective? Using the previously validated physics-based simulation model, both agents are trained under identical conditions with a reward that jointly penalizes tracking error and tension-constraint violation, and are evaluated across random, sinusoidal, and step disturbances using steady-state error, RMS, ISE, and IAE. The results show a consistent and interpretable trade-off: the stochastic SAC policy attains lower tracking error and better disturbance rejection, especially under time-varying and abrupt loads, at the cost of noisier control and longer training, whereas the deterministic DDPG policy converges faster and produces smoother torque and tension profiles but adapts less well to coupled disturbances. The study isolates the role of the exploration mechanism and the tension penalty in shaping these behaviors and offers practical guidance on selecting between deterministic and stochastic actor-critic methods for physically constrained, underactuated tendon-driven systems.

title: Reimagining consumer behaviour in retailing: An AI-adapted stimulus-organism-response model
abstract: Based on the classical Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) paradigm, this conceptual paper builds a theoretical model which proposes that AI-driven stimuli positively affect consumer satisfaction, purchase intention and repurchase intention. The paper takes a conceptual and theory building approach, bringing together literature on AI, retailing, and consumer behavior, and classical environmental-psychology theorising on the SOR paradigm to create a dual-pathway AI adapted SOR model in three iterative stages. There were two types of organismic paths in the model: a satisfaction-based path (security, ease of use, delivery, e-service, experience) and a purchase-intention-based path (AI-ease of use, pre-purchase satisfaction, online trust, previous experience) both leading to the repurchase intention, which were moderated by the technology readiness, privacy concern, algorithmic trust, and retail channel. The construction of a set of ten formal propositions which guide empirical testing. The model is conceptual and propositions are yet to be tested through the empirical studies. Structural equation modelling of the dual pathways, multi-group testing of the moderating propositions, and experimental testing of the moderating propositions, in addition to longitudinal designs testing the learning-based propositions of the model, all features among the priority areas. This paper is one of the first theoretical extensions of the SOR paradigm specific to adaptive, non-transparent, and channel-spanning nature of the AI-based retail stimuli, and transfers a distinct empirical literature into a single, falsifiable model.

title: Federated Learning and Generative AI for Privacy-Preserving Knowledge Transfer in Design Education
abstract: Cross-organizational design collaboration faces a fundamental paradox where enterprises possess valuable practical knowledge essential for student development, yet data privacy regulations prevent direct sharing. This study develops a federated learning-integrated generative AI platform addressing privacy-preserving knowledge transfer between industry and educational institutions while systematically enhancing student innovation capabilities. The platform employs a three-layer cloud-edge-end architecture incorporating dynamic quality-weighted federated aggregation with proximal regularization for non-IID heterogeneity, differential privacy mechanisms for formal privacy guarantees, and LoRA-adapted generative models for domain-specific design synthesis. Cross-domain knowledge fusion utilizes adversarial domain adaptation and knowledge distillation to harmonize heterogeneous expertise. Experiments on ShapeNet 3D dataset (51,300 models, 55 categories) demonstrate 72.3% classification accuracy with 23% communication overhead reduction compared to standard federated baselines. Generated designs achieve FID=22.7 and IS=3.79, validated through expert evaluation. Controlled educational trials with 42 students show significant capability improvements: design quality (+16.3 points), AI literacy (+25.6 points), and collaboration ability (+14.9 points), all statistically significant (p<0.01). This work pioneers the integration of federated learning with generative AI for design education, establishing a privacy-utility equilibrium that enables authentic industry knowledge exposure without raw data exchange, thereby advancing both collaborative innovation infrastructure and AI-literate design talent cultivation.
